title.zh: 卷一百九十 列傳第一百十五 三劉成杜鍾張王
title.en: Volume 190 Biographies 115: Three Liu's, Cheng, Du, Zhong, Zhang, Wang
title.raw: 卷一百九十 列傳第一百十五 三劉成杜鍾張王 Volume 190 Biographies 115: Three Liu's, Cheng, Du, Zhong, Zhang, Wang

sentences.zh: 三劉成杜鍾張王

translations.literal: The Three Liu's, Cheng, Du, Zhong, Zhang, Wang
translations.idiomatic: The Three Liu's, Cheng, Du, Zhong, Zhang, and Wang

sentences.zh: 劉建鋒

translations.literal: Liu Jianfeng
translations.idiomatic: Liu Jianfeng

sentences.zh: 劉建鋒，字銳端，蔡州朗山人。

translations.literal: Liu Jianfeng, courtesy name Ruiduan, was from Langshan in Caizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Jianfeng, courtesy name Ruiduan, was from Langshan in Caizhou.

sentences.zh: 為忠武軍部將，與孫儒、馬殷同事秦宗權。

translations.literal: He served as a subordinate general in the Zhongwu Army and, together with Sun Ru and Ma Yin, served Qin Zongquan.
translations.idiomatic: He served as a subordinate general in the Zhongwu Army and, together with Sun Ru and Ma Yin, served Qin Zongquan.

sentences.zh: 儒之敗，建鋒、殷收散卒，轉寇江西，有眾七千，推建鋒為主，殷為前鋒，張佶為謀主，略洪、虔數州，眾遂十餘萬。

translations.literal: After Sun Ru was defeated, Jianfeng and Ma Yin gathered scattered soldiers and turned to raiding Jiangxi. They had seven thousand men and put Jianfeng forward as leader, with Ma Yin as vanguard and Zhang Ji as strategist. They overran several prefectures including Hong and Qian, and their force grew to more than one hundred thousand.
translations.idiomatic: After Sun Ru was defeated, Jianfeng and Ma Yin gathered scattered soldiers and turned to raiding Jiangxi. They had seven thousand men and put Jianfeng forward as leader, with Ma Yin as vanguard and Zhang Ji as strategist. They overran several prefectures including Hong and Qian, and their force grew to more than one hundred thousand.

sentences.zh: 乾寧元年，取潭州，殺武安節度使鄧處訥，自稱節度留後，奉表京師，詔即拜檢校尚書左僕射、武安軍節度使。

translations.literal: In Qianning 1, he took Tanzhou, killed Deng Chuna, military governor of Wuan, called himself acting military governor, and sent a memorial to the capital. An edict thereupon appointed him acting Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs and military governor of the Wuan Army.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianning 1, he took Tanzhou, killed Deng Chuna, military governor of Wuan, called himself acting military governor, and sent a memorial to the capital. An edict thereupon appointed him acting Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs and military governor of the Wuan Army.

sentences.zh: 建鋒已得志，即嗜酒不事事。

translations.literal: Once Jianfeng had achieved his ambitions, he at once took to drink and neglected all affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Once Jianfeng had secured his position, he gave himself over to drink and ceased to attend to government.

sentences.zh: 新息小史陳贍為建鋒御者，妻美且艷，乃私之。

translations.literal: Chen Shan, a minor clerk of Xinxing, served as Jianfeng's charioteer; his wife was beautiful and seductive, and [Jianfeng] took her secretly.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Shan of Xinxing, a petty clerk whom Jianfeng employed as his driver, had a wife famed for her beauty—and Jianfeng carried on an affair with her in secret.

sentences.zh: 贍怒，袖鐵撾擊建鋒死，斷其喉。

translations.literal: Shan grew furious, concealed an iron mace in his sleeve, struck Jianfeng dead, and severed his throat.
translations.idiomatic: Enraged, Shan hid an iron mace in his sleeve, beat Jianfeng to death, and cut his throat.

sentences.zh: 眾推張佶為帥，佶固辭，馬踶傷佶左髀，下令曰：「吾非而主。」

translations.literal: The crowd pressed Zhang Ji to be commander-in-chief; Ji firmly declined; a horse kicked and wounded Ji's left thigh; he issued an order saying: "I am not your lord.
translations.idiomatic: The troops urged Zhang Ji to take command, but he stubbornly refused. A horse kicked him and injured his left thigh, and he declared, "I am not your leader.

sentences.zh: 時馬殷攻邵州未克，於是遣人迎殷，磔贍於市。

translations.literal: At that time Ma Yin was attacking Shaozhou but had not taken it; thereupon they sent someone to welcome Yin, and dismembered Shan in the marketplace.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Yin was then besieging Shaozhou without success, so they sent envoys to bring him in. Chen Shan was torn apart limb from limb in the public square.

sentences.zh: 殷至，佶坐受其謁。

translations.literal: When Yin arrived, Ji sat and received his obeisance.
translations.idiomatic: When Ma Yin arrived, Zhang Ji remained seated to receive his homage.

sentences.zh: 既而率將吏推殷為留後。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward he led the officers and clerks in pressing Yin to be acting military governor.
translations.idiomatic: He then led the commanders and officials in acclaiming Ma Yin as acting military governor.

sentences.zh: 詔即除檢校太傅、潭州刺史。

translations.literal: An edict at once appointed him acting Grand Preceptor and prefect of Tanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The throne immediately appointed him acting Grand Preceptor and prefect of Tanzhou.

sentences.zh: 殷以成汭、楊行密、劉隱皆養士以圖王霸，謂其屬高郁曰：「吾欲重幣以奉四鄰而固吾境，計安出？」

translations.literal: Yin, because Cheng Run, Yang Xingmi, and Liu Yin all maintained scholars to plot kingship and hegemony, said to his follower Gao Yu: "I wish to offer heavy gifts to honor the four neighboring states and secure my borders—what plan should we adopt?
translations.idiomatic: Seeing that Cheng Run, Yang Xingmi, and Liu Yin were all gathering men of talent in pursuit of empire, Ma Yin asked his adviser Gao Yu, "I mean to win over my neighbors with lavish gifts and firm up my frontiers. What course should we take?

sentences.zh: 郁曰：「荊南暗弱，焉能患我？

translations.literal: Yu said: "Jingnan is dim-witted and weak—how could it threaten us?
translations.idiomatic: Gao Yu replied, "Jingnan is feeble and shortsighted—it cannot menace us.

sentences.zh: 淮南，我讎也，固不吾援。

translations.literal: Huainan is my enemy; it certainly will not aid me.
translations.idiomatic: Huainan is our mortal foe and will never come to our aid.

sentences.zh: 公若置邸京師，歸天子職貢，王人來錫命，四方畏服，然後按兵討不廷，霸業成矣。」

translations.literal: If my lord establishes a residence in the capital, restores tribute duties to the Son of Heaven, and when the imperial envoy comes to bestow a commission the four quarters respect and submit—then afterward deploy troops to punish those who do not attend court, the work of hegemony will be accomplished."
translations.idiomatic: Establish a mission in the capital, resume regular tribute to the throne, and when imperial commissioners arrive with commissions the realm will submit in awe. Only then march against recalcitrant lords—and your supremacy will be secure."

sentences.zh: 殷悟，厚結宣武朱全忠以請於朝，乃拜湖南節度兵馬留後。

translations.literal: Yin understood; he bound himself closely to Xuanwu's Zhu Quanzhong to petition the court, and was then appointed acting military governor of Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Yin took the counsel to heart, cultivated Zhu Quanzhong of Xuanwu to intercede at court, and received appointment as acting military governor of Hunan.

sentences.zh: 郁又教殷鑄鉛鐵錢，十當銅錢一。

translations.literal: Yu also taught Yin to cast lead-iron coinage, ten of which equaled one copper coin.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Yu further urged Yin to mint lead-and-iron currency at a rate of ten to one against standard copper cash.

sentences.zh: 民得自摘山，收茗算，募高戶置邸閣居茗，號「八床主人」。

translations.literal: The people were permitted to pick tea mountains on their own; tea levies were collected; wealthy households were recruited to set up lodges to store tea, titled "Lords of the Eight Beds."
translations.idiomatic: Private citizens were allowed to harvest mountain tea on their own account; the state levied a tea tax; and wealthy patrons were enlisted to run lodging-houses for storing tea, styled "Masters of the Eight Couch-Beds."

sentences.zh: 歲入算數十萬，用度遂饒。

translations.literal: Annual revenue from these levies reached several hundred thousand, and expenditures became ample.
translations.idiomatic: Annual receipts ran into the hundreds of thousands, and the treasury grew flush.

sentences.zh: 於是收邵、衡、永、道、郴、連六州，進攻桂州，執留後劉士政。

translations.literal: Thereupon he seized the six prefectures Shao, Heng, Yong, Dao, Chen, and Lian, advanced to attack Guizhou, and captured acting governor Liu Shizheng.
translations.idiomatic: He then secured Shao, Heng, Yong, Dao, Chen, and Lian, marched on Guizhou, and took the acting governor Liu Shizheng prisoner.

sentences.zh: 諸城望風奔潰，盡得昭、賀、梧、象、柳、宜、蒙等州。

translations.literal: The various cities fled and collapsed at the mere sight of his banners; he obtained in full the prefectures Zhao, He, Wu, Xiang, Liu, Yi, Meng, and others.
translations.idiomatic: City after city capitulated before his columns, and he brought Zhao, He, Wu, Xiang, Liu, Yi, Meng, and the rest under his control.

sentences.zh: 又攻容管，執寧遠節度使龐巨曦，虜其眾及貲。

translations.literal: He also attacked Rongguan, seized Ningyuan military governor Pang Juxi, and captured his troops and goods.
translations.idiomatic: He further invaded Rongguan, took the Ningyuan military governor Pang Juxi captive, and carried off his soldiers and stores.

sentences.zh: 昭宗在鳳翔，難方亟，遣中人間道賜朱書，密詔使殷與楊行密攻汴州，殷兵訖不出。

translations.literal: Emperor Zhaozong was at Fengxiang; troubles pressed from all sides; he sent a eunuch by a secret route to bestow a vermilion writ, secretly instructing Yin and Yang Xingmi to attack Bianzhou—but Yin's troops in the end never marched out.
translations.idiomatic: With Emperor Zhaozong besieged at Fengxiang and calamities closing in on every side, a eunuch was dispatched by a hidden route with an imperial letter in vermilion ink, secretly ordering Ma Yin and Yang Xingmi to strike Bianzhou. Yin's army never stirred.

sentences.zh: 殷弟賨，沈勇知書史，從孫儒為盜，晚事楊行密為黑雲軍使。

translations.literal: Yin's younger brother Cong was deep and brave and versed in books and history; he followed Sun Ru as a bandit, and later served Yang Xingmi as commander of the Black Cloud Army.
translations.idiomatic: Yin's younger brother Ma Cong was a man of depth and courage, well read in history. He had ridden with the bandit Sun Ru and later entered Yang Xingmi's service as commander of the Black Cloud Army.

sentences.zh: 與錢镠戰，數有功。

translations.literal: In fighting Qian Liu he scored many achievements.
translations.idiomatic: Campaigning against Qian Liu, he won repeated distinction.

sentences.zh: 夜臥，常有光怪。

translations.literal: When he lay down at night, strange lights often appeared.
translations.idiomatic: At night in his sleep, uncanny lights would often flare about him.

sentences.zh: 行密知之，曰：「吾今歸汝於兄。」

translations.literal: Xingmi knew of this and said: "I now return you to your elder brother.
translations.idiomatic: Xingmi took note of this and said, "I am sending you back to your brother.

sentences.zh: 辭曰：「賨一敗卒，公待以不死。

translations.literal: He declined, saying: "Cong is but a defeated soldier; my lord treated me as one not to be put to death.
translations.idiomatic: Cong demurred: "I was only a beaten fugitive, yet you spared my life.

sentences.zh: 湖南在宇下，朝亡夕至，但誼不忍舍公。」

translations.literal: Hunan lies beneath your canopy; it may perish in the morning and reach you by evening—only that I cannot bear to abandon my lord out of duty."
translations.idiomatic: Hunan lies at your doorstep—it could fall by morning and be at your gates by nightfall. Yet loyalty will not let me leave your service."

sentences.zh: 行密具賫以遣曰：「爾還，與兄共食湘、楚，然何以報我？」

translations.literal: Xingmi fully prepared gifts and sent him off, saying: "You return to share Xiang and Chu with your brother—yet how will you repay me?"
translations.idiomatic: Xingmi furnished him with lavish gifts for the journey and asked, "You will go home to share Hunan and Chu with your brother—but what will you do for me in return?"

sentences.zh: 答曰：「願通二國好，使商賈相資。」

translations.literal: He answered: "I wish to open good relations between our two states and let merchants support one another."
translations.idiomatic: He answered, "I shall open friendly ties between our realms and let merchants trade freely across our borders."

sentences.zh: 行密喜。

translations.literal: Xingmi was pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Xingmi was delighted.

sentences.zh: 既至，殷表以自副。

translations.literal: Once he arrived, Yin memorialized to appoint him his own deputy.
translations.idiomatic: On his arrival, Ma Yin petitioned the court to name him his own deputy.

sentences.zh: 每勸殷與行密連和，殷畏全忠，卒不克。

translations.literal: He repeatedly urged Yin to ally with Xingmi; Yin feared Quanzhong, and in the end could not do it.
translations.idiomatic: He repeatedly urged Ma Yin to ally with Yang Xingmi, but Yin feared Zhu Quanzhong and never managed it.

sentences.zh: 殷與建鋒同里人，凡宗權黨散為盜者，皆以酷烈相矜，時通名「蔡賊」云。

translations.literal: Yin and Jianfeng were men of the same village; all who had scattered from Zongquan's faction to become bandits prided themselves on cruelty and severity, and were commonly called "the Cai bandits."
translations.idiomatic: Ma Yin and Liu Jianfeng were fellow townsmen. The scattered followers of Qin Zongquan who turned to brigandage all boasted of their ruthlessness and were known collectively as "the Cai bandits."

sentences.zh: 成汭，青州人。

translations.literal: Cheng Run was a man of Qingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Run was a native of Qingzhou.

sentences.zh: 少無行，使酒殺人，亡為浮屠。

translations.literal: In youth he was without propriety; given to drink he killed a man and fled to become a Buddhist monk.
translations.idiomatic: In his youth he was dissolute; in a drunken rage he killed a man and fled, taking refuge as a Buddhist monk.

sentences.zh: 後入蔡賊中，為賊帥假子，更姓名為郭禹。

translations.literal: Later he entered among the Cai bandits, became a bandit chieftain's adopted son, and changed his name to Guo Yu.
translations.idiomatic: He later joined the Cai bandits, was adopted as a son by a rebel leader, and took the name Guo Yu.

sentences.zh: 當戍江陵，亡為盜，保火門山。

translations.literal: When he was to garrison Jiangling he fled and became a bandit, holding Huomen Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: While posted to garrison Jiangling he deserted to banditry and seized Huomen Mountain as his stronghold.

sentences.zh: 後詣荊南節度使陳儒降，署裨校。

translations.literal: Later he went to Jingnan military governor Chen Ru to surrender and was appointed a staff officer.
translations.idiomatic: He later surrendered to the Jingnan military governor Chen Ru and was given a post as staff officer.

sentences.zh: 久之，張瑰囚儒，以禹凶慓，欲殺之。

translations.literal: After a long while Zhang Gui imprisoned Ru; because Yu was fierce and violent, he wished to kill him.
translations.idiomatic: In time Zhang Gui imprisoned Chen Ru and, deeming Guo Yu dangerously fierce, meant to execute him.

sentences.zh: 禹結千人奔入峽，夜有蛇環其所，祝曰：「有所負者，死生唯命。」

translations.literal: Yu gathered a thousand men and fled into the gorges; at night a serpent coiled about his place; he prayed: "If I have done wrong, life and death are only fate.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Yu rallied a thousand men and fled into the gorges. That night a serpent coiled about his camp, and he prayed: "If I am guilty of some wrong, let fate decide whether I live or die.

sentences.zh: 既而蛇亡。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward the serpent vanished.
translations.idiomatic: The serpent soon slithered away.

sentences.zh: 禹乃襲歸州，入之，自稱刺史。

translations.literal: Yu then raided Guizhou, entered it, and styled himself prefect.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Yu then stormed Guizhou, took the city, and proclaimed himself prefect.

sentences.zh: 招還流亡，訓士伍，得勝兵三千，秦宗權故將許存奔禹，禹以青州剽卒三百畀之，使討荊南部將牟權於清江，禽權，取其眾。

translations.literal: He summoned back the displaced, trained soldiers, and obtained three thousand seasoned troops; Qin Zongquan's former general Xu Cun fled to Yu; Yu gave him three hundred Qingzhou raiders and sent him to attack Jingnan's subordinate general Mou Quan at Qingjiang, capturing Quan and taking his forces.
translations.idiomatic: He recalled exiles, drilled his troops, and mustered three thousand battle-ready soldiers. Xu Cun, a former officer of Qin Zongquan, came over to him; Guo Yu gave him three hundred Qingzhou raiders and sent him against the Jingnan subordinate Mou Quan at Qingjiang. Xu Cun captured Mou Quan and absorbed his troops.

sentences.zh: 禹又破其將王建肇，建肇奔黔州。

translations.literal: Yu also defeated his general Wang Jianzhao; Jianzhao fled to Qianzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Yu also routed the general Wang Jianzhao, who fled to Qianzhou.

sentences.zh: 昭宗拜禹荊南節度留後，始改名汭，復故姓。

translations.literal: Emperor Zhaozong appointed Yu acting military governor of Jingnan; he then first changed his name to Run and restored his original surname.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Zhaozong appointed him acting military governor of Jingnan. He then adopted the name Run and reclaimed his birth surname.

sentences.zh: 宗權餘黨常厚攻夔州。

translations.literal: A remnant of Zongquan's faction, Chang Hou, attacked Kuizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Chang Hou, a survivor of Qin Zongquan's faction, attacked Kuizhou.

sentences.zh: 是時，西川節度使王建遣將屯忠州，與夔州刺史毛湘相唇齒，厚屯白帝。

translations.literal: At this time Xichuan military governor Wang Jian sent a general to garrison Zhongzhou, lip-to-teeth with Kuizhou prefect Mao Xiang; Hou encamped at Baidi.
translations.idiomatic: The Xichuan military governor Wang Jian had posted a general at Zhongzhou in mutual support with Kuizhou prefect Mao Xiang, while Chang Hou held Baidi.

sentences.zh: 汭率存乘二軍之間攻之，二軍使人誶辱汭，韓楚言尤劇，汭恥之曰：「有如禽賊，當支解以逞！」

translations.literal: Run led Cun to attack between the two armies; the two armies sent men to revile Run; Han Chuyan's words were especially harsh; Run, shamed, said: "If I capture the bandits, I shall dismember them to vent my wrath!
translations.idiomatic: Run led Xu Cun to strike between the two enemy forces. Envoys from both camps heaped abuse on Run, Han Chuyan's insults the bitterest of all. Stung to shame, Run swore, "If I take these rebels alive, I shall tear them limb from limb!

sentences.zh: 會存夜斬營襲厚，破之，厚奔萬州，為刺史張造所拒，走綿州。

translations.literal: It happened that Cun by night cut through the camp and raided Hou, defeating him; Hou fled to Wanzhou, was refused by prefect Zhang Zao, and fled to Mianzhou.
translations.idiomatic: That night Xu Cun cut through the enemy camp and routed Chang Hou. Hou fled to Wanzhou, was turned away by the prefect Zhang Zao, and retreated to Mianzhou.

sentences.zh: 存入夔州。

translations.literal: Cun entered Kuizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Cun then entered Kuizhou.

sentences.zh: 楚言妻李語夫曰：「君常辱軍，且支解，不如前死。」

translations.literal: Chuyan's wife Li spoke to her husband: "You constantly insult the army, and will be dismembered—better to die beforehand.
translations.idiomatic: Chuyan's wife Li told her husband, "You have heaped insults on the army, and Run has sworn to tear you apart. Better to die now than face that fate.

sentences.zh: 楚言不決。

translations.literal: Chuyan could not decide.
translations.idiomatic: Chuyan could not make up his mind.

sentences.zh: 李礪刀席下，方共食，復語之，夫曰：「未可知。」

translations.literal: Li sharpened a knife beneath the mat; as they were eating together she spoke to him again; her husband said: "It is not yet certain.
translations.idiomatic: Li honed a knife beneath their mat. While they were still at table she pressed him again, and he said, "The outcome is not yet certain.

sentences.zh: 李取刀斷其首，並殺三子，乃自剄。

translations.literal: Li took the knife and severed his head, also killed their three sons, and then cut her own throat.
translations.idiomatic: Li seized the blade, struck off his head, killed their three sons as well, and then cut her own throat.

sentences.zh: 汭畏其烈，禮葬之，刻石表曰烈女。

translations.literal: Run feared her fierceness, buried them with ceremony, and carved a stone tablet titled "A Fierce Woman."
translations.idiomatic: Run, awed by her resolve, gave them honorable burial and set up a stone tablet inscribed "A Woman of Fierce Virtue."

sentences.zh: 即使司馬劉昌美守夔，率存溯江略雲安，建將皆奔。

translations.literal: He then sent Chief Administrator Liu Changmei to hold Kuizhou, led Cun upriver to seize Yun'an, and Wang Jian's generals all fled.
translations.idiomatic: He appointed Chief Administrator Liu Changmei to hold Kuizhou and led Xu Cun upriver to overrun Yun'an. Wang Jian's generals all fled.

sentences.zh: 存按兵渝州，盡下瀕江州縣。

translations.literal: Cun held his army at Yuzhou and took all the prefectures and counties along the river.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Cun held his forces at Yuzhou and brought every riverside prefecture and county under his control.

sentences.zh: 時王建肇據黔州自守，帝以建肇為武泰軍節度使。

translations.literal: At this time Wang Jianzhao held Qianzhou in self-defense; the emperor appointed Jianzhao military governor of the Wutai Army.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jianzhao was then holding Qianzhou on his own authority, and the throne appointed him military governor of the Wutai Army.

sentences.zh: 汭遣將趙武率存攻之，建肇走，汭乃以武為留後，存為萬州刺史。

translations.literal: Run sent the general Zhao Wu leading Cun to attack him; Jianzhao fled; Run then made Wu acting governor and Cun prefect of Wanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Run dispatched Zhao Wu with Xu Cun to attack him. Jianzhao fled, and Run appointed Wu acting governor while making Xu Cun prefect of Wanzhou.

sentences.zh: 存不得志，汭遣客伺之，方蹴球，汭曰：「存必叛，自試其力矣。」

translations.literal: Cun was discontent; Run sent a guest to watch him; just as he was kicking a ball, Run said: "Cun is sure to rebel—he is testing his strength.
translations.idiomatic: Dissatisfied with his lot, Xu Cun drew Run's suspicion. A spy reported that he was playing cuju, and Run said, "He is certain to rebel—he is testing how strong he still is.

sentences.zh: 遣將襲之。

translations.literal: He sent a general to raid him.
translations.idiomatic: Run sent troops to strike him down.

sentences.zh: 存夜率左右超堞走，與王建肇皆降於王建。

translations.literal: By night Cun led his close followers over the battlements and fled; he and Wang Jianzhao both surrendered to Wang Jian.
translations.idiomatic: Cun fled by night with his personal guard over the city wall. He and Wang Jianzhao both submitted to Wang Jian.

sentences.zh: 汭頗知吏治，嘗錄囚，盡其情。

translations.literal: Run was quite skilled in governing through officials; he once reviewed prisoners and brought out the full truth in each case.
translations.idiomatic: Run was notably adept at administration. Once, reviewing prisoners, he drew out the full truth in every case.

sentences.zh: 墊江賊陰殺令，其主簿疑小史導之，訊不承。

translations.literal: Bandits in Dianjiang secretly killed the magistrate; the chief clerk suspected a petty clerk had guided them; under interrogation he would not confess.
translations.idiomatic: Bandits in Dianjiang had secretly murdered the magistrate. The chief clerk suspected a petty clerk had guided them, but interrogation failed to extract a confession.

sentences.zh: 臨刑曰：「我且訟地下。」

translations.literal: Facing execution he said: "I shall yet bring suit in the underworld.
translations.idiomatic: On the scaffold he cried, "I will bring my case before the judges of the dead!

sentences.zh: 逾月，吏暴死。

translations.literal: After more than a month the clerk died suddenly.
translations.idiomatic: Within a month the clerk died suddenly.

sentences.zh: 汭聞，益詳於獄。

translations.literal: When Run heard of it, he became still more thorough in prisons.
translations.idiomatic: When Run heard of it, he became still more meticulous in his handling of criminal cases.

sentences.zh: 始治州，民版無幾，未再期，自占者萬餘。

translations.literal: When he first governed the prefecture, household registers were few; before two years had passed, those who registered themselves exceeded ten thousand.
translations.idiomatic: When he first took charge of the prefecture, registered households were few. In less than two years, voluntary registrants exceeded ten thousand.

sentences.zh: 帝數詔刻石頌功，輒固辭。

translations.literal: The emperor repeatedly ordered stone inscriptions to praise his achievements, but he firmly declined each time.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor repeatedly ordered stone monuments to praise his achievements, but Run steadfastly refused.

sentences.zh: 時鎮國節度使韓建亦以治顯，號「北韓南郭」。

translations.literal: At the time Zhenguo military governor Han Jian was also famed for his governance; they were called "Han in the north, Guo in the south."
translations.idiomatic: The Zhenguo military governor Han Jian was likewise famed for good government, and the two were styled "Han in the north, Guo in the south."

sentences.zh: 汭進累檢校太尉、中書令、上谷郡王。

translations.literal: Run was promoted in succession to acting Grand Commandant, Director of the Secretariat, and Prince of Shanggu Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Run rose through successive appointments to acting Grand Commandant, Director of the Secretariat, and Prince of Shanggu Commandery.

sentences.zh: 雲安榷鹽，本隸鹽鐵，汭擅取之，故能畜兵五萬。

translations.literal: The salt monopoly at Yun'an originally belonged to the Salt and Iron Commission; Run seized it on his own authority, and so was able to maintain an army of fifty thousand.
translations.idiomatic: The salt monopoly at Yun'an had belonged to the Salt and Iron Commission, but Run seized it for himself and thereby sustained an army of fifty thousand.

sentences.zh: 初任賀隱，隱，賢者也，故汭所舉少過。

translations.literal: At first he employed He Yin; Yin was a worthy man, and so Run's recommendations were rarely in error.
translations.idiomatic: At first he relied on He Yin, a man of talent, and so Run's appointments were rarely mistaken.

sentences.zh: 晚得妻父任之，譖害諸子，汭皆手殺之，至絕嗣。

translations.literal: In his later years he obtained his wife's father Ren Zhi, who slandered and harmed his sons; Run personally killed them all, even to the extinction of his line.
translations.idiomatic: In his later years he took up his father-in-law Ren Zhi, who slandered and destroyed his sons. Run killed them all with his own hand, leaving himself without heirs.

sentences.zh: 澧、朗本荊南隸州，為雷滿所據，別為節度，汭數請之，宰相徐彥若不許。

translations.literal: Li and Lang had originally been subordinate prefectures of Jingnan; they were seized by Lei Man and made a separate military governorship; Run repeatedly petitioned for them, but chief minister Xu Yanru would not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: Li and Lang had once been subordinate prefectures of Jingnan, but Lei Man seized them and made them a separate command. Run petitioned repeatedly for their return, but the chief minister Xu Yanru refused.

sentences.zh: 及彥若罷，道江陵，汭出怨言，彥若曰：「公專一面，自視桓、文，一賊不能取，而怨朝廷乎？」

translations.literal: When Yanru was dismissed and passed through Jiangling, Run uttered complaints; Yanru said: "My lord monopolizes one region and regards himself as Huan and Wen—yet cannot take a single bandit, and blames the court?
translations.idiomatic: When Yanru was dismissed and passed through Jiangling, Run voiced his grievances. Yanru replied, "You hold a realm of your own and fancy yourself a Duke of Huan or Wen—yet you cannot subdue a single bandit, and you blame the court?

sentences.zh: 汭大慚。

translations.literal: Run was deeply ashamed.
translations.idiomatic: Run was deeply shamed.

sentences.zh: 晚喜術士，餌藥濱死而蘇。

translations.literal: In his later years he delighted in magicians, took their drugs, nearly died at the water's edge, and revived.
translations.idiomatic: In his later years he dabbled with magicians, swallowed their elixirs, nearly died, and was revived.

sentences.zh: 天復三年，帝詔淮南節度使楊行密圍鄂州，朱全忠使韓救之，諷汭與馬殷、雷彥威掎角。

translations.literal: In the third year of Tianfu the emperor ordered Huainan military governor Yang Xingmi to besiege Ezhou; Zhu Quanzhong sent Han to rescue it and urged Run, Ma Yin, and Lei Yanwei to coordinate pincer attacks.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Tianfu the emperor ordered Yang Xingmi of Huainan to besiege Ezhou. Zhu Quanzhong sent Han to relieve the city and urged Run, Ma Yin, and Lei Yanwei to strike in concert from several directions.

sentences.zh: 汭身自將而行，下知汭不足亢行密，無敢諫，唯親吏楊師厚勸之。

translations.literal: Run personally led the army on the march; his subordinates knew Run could not stand against Xingmi and dared not remonstrate—only his intimate clerk Yang Shihou urged him on.
translations.idiomatic: Run took the field in person. His officers knew he was no match for Yang Xingmi and dared not dissuade him—only his trusted aide Yang Shihou encouraged him to press on.

sentences.zh: 汭為巨艦，堂皇悉備，行至公安，卜不吉，欲還，師厚曰：「公舉全軍，中道還，何以見百姓？」

translations.literal: Run built great warships, grand and fully equipped; when he reached Gong'an, divination was inauspicious and he wished to return; Shihou said: "My lord has raised the whole army—if you turn back halfway, how will you face the people?
translations.idiomatic: Run fitted out enormous warships, splendid in every detail. At Gong'an the omens turned ill and he wished to turn back. Shihou said, "You have committed your entire force—how can you face the people if you retreat halfway?

sentences.zh: 汭乃行。

translations.literal: Run then advanced.
translations.idiomatic: Run pressed on.

sentences.zh: 彥威潛師略江陵，汭諸將念私，無鬥志。

translations.literal: Yanwei secretly sent troops to raid Jiangling; Run's generals thought of private interests and had no fighting spirit.
translations.idiomatic: Yanwei secretly sent troops against Jiangling. Run's generals were preoccupied with private concerns and had no heart for battle.

sentences.zh: 淮南將李神福壁沙橋，望汭軍曰：「戰艦雖盛，首尾斷絕，可取也。」

translations.literal: Huainan general Li Shenfu fortified Shaqiao, looked at Run's army and said: "Though the warships are grand, head and tail are cut off—they can be taken.
translations.idiomatic: The Huainan general Li Shenfu fortified Shaqiao, surveyed Run's fleet, and said, "Their warships may be imposing, but the line is broken at both ends—they can be taken.

sentences.zh: 擊汭君山，敗之，火其船，眾大潰，汭投江死，士民皆為彥威所劫。

translations.literal: He struck Run at Junshan, defeated him, set fire to his ships; the host collapsed in great disorder; Run threw himself into the river and died; soldiers and civilians were all plundered by Yanwei.
translations.idiomatic: He attacked Run at Junshan, routed him, and burned his ships. The army broke in panic. Run threw himself into the river and drowned. Soldiers and civilians alike were plundered by Yanwei.

sentences.zh: 韓走還。

translations.literal: Han fled back.
translations.idiomatic: Han fled homeward.

sentences.zh: 王建遂取夔、施、忠、萬四州。

translations.literal: Wang Jian then took the four prefectures Kui, Shi, Zhong, and Wan.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jian then seized Kui, Shi, Zhong, and Wan.

sentences.zh: 天祐中，全忠表汭死國事，請與杜洪皆立廟云。

translations.literal: During Tianyou, Quanzhong memorialized that Run had died in service to the state and requested that temples be established for him and Du Hong alike.
translations.idiomatic: During the Tianyou reign, Zhu Quanzhong petitioned that Run had died in the state's service and asked that temples be erected for both him and Du Hong.

sentences.zh: 杜洪，鄂州人。

translations.literal: Du Hong was a man of Ezhou.
translations.idiomatic: Du Hong was a native of Ezhou.

sentences.zh: 為裏俳兒。

translations.literal: He was a village performer.
translations.idiomatic: He began as a village entertainer.

sentences.zh: 乾符末，黃巢亂江南，永興民皆亡為盜。

translations.literal: At the end of Qianfu, Huang Chao threw Jiangnan into chaos; the people of Yongxing all fled and became bandits.
translations.idiomatic: At the close of the Qianfu era Huang Chao ravaged the south, and the people of Yongxing fled wholesale into banditry.

sentences.zh: 刺史崔紹募民強雄者為土團軍，賊不敢侵，於是人人知兵。

translations.literal: Prefect Cui Shao recruited the strongest among the people as local militia; bandits dared not invade, and thereafter everyone knew warfare.
translations.idiomatic: The prefect Cui Shao recruited the sturdiest men among the populace into local militia units. Bandits no longer dared attack, and soon every man knew how to fight.

sentences.zh: 杭州刺史路審中為董昌所拒，走客黃州。

translations.literal: Hangzhou prefect Lu Shenzhong was repelled by Dong Chang and fled as a guest to Huangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The Hangzhou prefect Lu Shenzhong was driven out by Dong Chang and took refuge at Huangzhou.

sentences.zh: 中和末，聞紹卒，募士三千入鄂州以守。

translations.literal: At the end of Zhonghe, hearing that Shao had died, he recruited three thousand men and entered Ezhou to defend it.
translations.idiomatic: At the close of the Zhonghe era, hearing that Cui Shao had died, he raised three thousand men and marched into Ezhou to hold it.

sentences.zh: 洪為州將，有功，亦逐岳州刺史居之。

translations.literal: Hong was a commander of the prefecture with achievements, and also drove out the Yuezhou prefect and occupied it.
translations.idiomatic: Hong was a prefectural officer who had distinguished himself in service and also drove out the Yuezhou prefect and seized that post.

sentences.zh: 光啟二年，安陸賊周通率兵攻審中，審中亡去，洪乘虛入鄂，自為節度留後，僖宗即拜本軍節度使。

translations.literal: In the second year of Guangqi, Anlu bandit Zhou Tong led troops to attack Shenzhong; Shenzhong fled; Hong seized the opening and entered E, styled himself acting military governor, and Emperor Xizong at once appointed him military governor of this army.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Guangqi the Anlu bandit Zhou Tong attacked Lu Shenzhong, who fled. Hong seized the moment, entered Ezhou, and proclaimed himself acting military governor. Emperor Xizong immediately confirmed him as military governor of the command.

sentences.zh: 是時，永興民吳討據黃州，駱殷據永興，二人皆隸土團者也，故軍剽甚。

translations.literal: At this time Yongxing native Wu Tao held Huangzhou and Luo Yin held Yongxing; both had belonged to the local militia, and so their armies were extremely predatory.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Tao of Yongxing held Huangzhou and Luo Yin held Yongxing itself. Both had risen from the local militia, and their forces were savagely predatory.

sentences.zh: 洪雖得節制，而附朱全忠，絕東南貢路。

translations.literal: Although Hong obtained the military commission, he attached himself to Zhu Quanzhong and cut off the southeastern tribute route.
translations.idiomatic: Though Hong had won his commission, he attached himself to Zhu Quanzhong and severed the southeastern tribute route.

sentences.zh: 乾寧初，身自將擊討，乞師淮南，楊行密遣朱延壽助之。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Qianning he personally led troops to attack Tao, begged troops from Huainan, and Yang Xingmi sent Zhu Yanshou to aid him.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Qianning he took the field in person against Wu Tao, sought aid from Huainan, and Yang Xingmi sent Zhu Yanshou to reinforce him.

sentences.zh: 洪引還，延壽拔黃州，俘討獻京師。

translations.literal: Hong led his army back; Yanshou took Huangzhou, captured Tao, and sent him to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Hong withdrew his forces. Zhu Yanshou seized Huangzhou, took Wu Tao prisoner, and sent him to the capital.

sentences.zh: 駱殷棄永興走，行密取其地。

translations.literal: Luo Yin abandoned Yongxing and fled; Xingmi took his territory.
translations.idiomatic: Luo Yin abandoned Yongxing and fled, and Yang Xingmi seized his territory.

sentences.zh: 洪得駱殷，倚為心腹，間取永興守之。

translations.literal: Hong obtained Luo Yin, relied on him as intimate confidant, and from time to time took Yongxing for him to guard.
translations.idiomatic: Hong won Luo Yin over as a trusted confidant and periodically sent him to hold Yongxing.

sentences.zh: 全忠方圍鳳翔，昭宗遣使者東出，道武昌，洪皆殺之。

translations.literal: Quanzhong was then besieging Fengxiang; Zhaozong sent envoys east; passing through Wuchang, Hong killed them all.
translations.idiomatic: While Zhu Quanzhong was besieging Fengxiang, Emperor Zhaozong sent envoys eastward. Every one who passed through Wuchang was killed by Hong.

sentences.zh: 時行密略光州，詔洪出兵，與忠義趙匡凝、武安馬殷襲安州。

translations.literal: At this time Xingmi was seizing Guangzhou; an edict ordered Hong to march out, and together with Zhongyi's Zhao Kuangning and Wu'an's Ma Yin to raid Anzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Xingmi was then overrunning Guangzhou. An imperial edict ordered Hong to take the field jointly with Zhao Kuangning of Zhongyi and Ma Yin of Wu'an for a strike against Anzhou.

sentences.zh: 行密使李神福、劉存率舟師萬人討洪，駱殷棄永興走，縣民方詔守以待命。

translations.literal: Xingmi sent Li Shenfu and Liu Cun leading ten thousand naval troops to attack Hong; Luo Yin abandoned Yongxing and fled; the county people had Fang Zhao guard it awaiting orders.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Xingmi dispatched Li Shenfu and Liu Cun with ten thousand men by water against Hong. Luo Yin fled Yongxing, leaving Fang Zhao and the county militia to hold the town pending further orders.

sentences.zh: 神福已得詔，大喜，以永興壯縣，饋餫所仰，既得，鄂半矣，遂進圍鄂州。

translations.literal: Shenfu had already won Zhao over and was greatly pleased; because Yongxing was a strong county on which supplies depended, once he obtained it half of E was his—thereupon he advanced to besiege Ezhou.
translations.idiomatic: Shenfu had already won Fang Zhao's submission and was overjoyed. Yongxing was a prosperous county on which his supply lines depended; with it in hand, he held half of Hong's realm, and he pressed on to besiege Ezhou.

sentences.zh: 洪嬰城，請救於汴，全忠率兵五萬營霍丘。

translations.literal: Hong shut himself in the city and begged rescue from Bian; Quanzhong led fifty thousand troops to camp at Huoqiu.
translations.idiomatic: Hong shut himself within the walls and appealed to Bian for relief. Zhu Quanzhong marched fifty thousand men to encamp at Huoqiu.

sentences.zh: 行密禦之，汴兵不利，引還，使別將吳章以三千兵解圍，神福迎破之。

translations.literal: Xingmi opposed them; the Bian troops fared poorly and withdrew; he sent the subordinate general Wu Zhang with three thousand men to lift the siege; Shenfu went out to meet and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Xingmi met them in battle. The Bian forces fared poorly and withdrew, but Quanzhong sent Wu Zhang with three thousand men to relieve the siege. Shenfu sallied forth and routed them.

sentences.zh: 時全忠方與河東軍薄戰，故不能救洪。

translations.literal: At this time Quanzhong was locked in close combat with the Hedong army and so could not rescue Hong.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Quanzhong was then locked in close combat with the Hedong army and could not rescue Hong.

sentences.zh: 洪乃求助於馬殷，殷不答。

translations.literal: Hong then sought help from Ma Yin; Yin did not answer.
translations.idiomatic: Hong then appealed to Ma Yin, who gave no reply.

sentences.zh: 洪計窮，復走全忠，全忠遣曹延祚合吳章兵萬三千救洪。

translations.literal: Hong's plans were exhausted; he fled again to Quanzhong; Quanzhong sent Cao Yanzuo combining with Wu Zhang's troops to thirteen thousand to rescue Hong.
translations.idiomatic: With his options exhausted, Hong fled once more to Zhu Quanzhong, who sent Cao Yanzuo with Wu Zhang's forces—thirteen thousand men in all—to relieve him.

sentences.zh: 淮南將劉存浚坎傅城。

translations.literal: The Huainan general Liu Cun dug a trench around Fu city.
translations.idiomatic: The Huainan general Liu Cun dug siege trenches around the outer works.

sentences.zh: 殷為洪謀曰：「淮兵深入，仰永興以濟，若奇兵取之，賊不戰而潰。」

translations.literal: Yin devised a plan for Hong, saying: "The Huainan troops have penetrated deep and rely on Yongxing for supplies; if a surprise force takes it, the bandits will collapse without fighting.
translations.idiomatic: Luo Yin advised Hong: "The Huainan army has pushed deep inland and depends on Yongxing for supplies. Send a surprise force against Yongxing and they will collapse without a battle.

sentences.zh: 洪以精兵合汴人間道掩永興，三十里而舍。

translations.literal: Hong led elite troops combined with Bian men by a secret route to surprise Yongxing, and encamped thirty li away.
translations.idiomatic: Hong led his best troops with the Bian relief force along a hidden route against Yongxing and encamped thirty li away.

sentences.zh: 存以方詔、苗璘當之。

translations.literal: Cun assigned Fang Zhao and Miao Lin to face them.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Cun posted Fang Zhao and Miao Lin to meet them.

sentences.zh: 汴亡卒走淮壁，言軍虛實曰：「鄆軍懦，可取，開道軍不可當也。」

translations.literal: Bian deserters fled to the Huainan ramparts and reported the army's true condition, saying: "The Yan troops are cowardly and can be taken; the Kaodao troops cannot be faced.
translations.idiomatic: Bian deserters reached the Huainan camp and reported on enemy dispositions: "The Yan contingent is timid and can be taken; the Kaodao contingent is not to be faced head-on.

sentences.zh: 璘曰：「殺強則弱者撓矣。」

translations.literal: Lin said: "Kill the strong and the weak will waver."
translations.idiomatic: Miao Lin said, "Strike down the strong and the weak will lose heart."

sentences.zh: 乃自擊開道軍，敗之，禽汴士三百人，徇城下。

translations.literal: He then personally attacked the Kaodao army, defeated it, captured three hundred Bian soldiers, and displayed them below the city.
translations.idiomatic: He led the assault on the Kaodao contingent himself, routed it, took three hundred Bian soldiers prisoner, and paraded them beneath the walls.

sentences.zh: 洪軍氣沮，存使辯士臨說，洪恃汴方強，無降意。

translations.literal: Hong's army's spirit sank; Cun sent an eloquent persuader to speak to him from afar; Hong relied on Bian's present strength and had no intent to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Hong's army lost heart. Liu Cun sent an eloquent envoy to negotiate, but Hong still counted on Bian's strength and would not consider surrender.

sentences.zh: 或勸存急擊援兵，則城自下，存曰：「擊之，賊入，則城固矣；

translations.literal: Some urged Cun to attack the relief troops quickly, then the city would fall of itself; Cun said: "If we attack, the bandits will enter and the city will become solid;
translations.idiomatic: Some urged Liu Cun to strike the relief force at once so the city would fall of itself. Cun replied, "If we attack now, the enemy will pour into the city and make it impregnable.

sentences.zh: 若縱其遁，城可取也。」

translations.literal: if we let them escape, the city can be taken.
translations.idiomatic: If we let them flee, the city can be taken.

sentences.zh: 俄而汴軍走，是日城陷，執洪及曹延祚，窮斬其餘。

translations.literal: Shortly the Bian army fled; that same day the city fell; Hong and Cao Yanzuo were captured, and the rest were hunted down and executed.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the Bian army broke and fled. That same day the city fell. Hong and Cao Yanzuo were taken prisoner, and the rest were hunted down and slaughtered to the last man.

sentences.zh: 行密見洪，責曰：「爾同逆賊弒主，與孤為仇，吾軍還，而復為賊後拒，今定何如？」

translations.literal: Xingmi saw Hong and reproached him: "You joined the rebel bandits in murdering the sovereign, made yourself my enemy; when my army returned you again blocked the rebels' rear—what is settled now?
translations.idiomatic: Yang Xingmi confronted Hong and rebuked him: "You sided with rebels who murdered the emperor and made yourself my enemy. When my army withdrew, you again barred my path at the rebels' rear. What is there to settle now?

sentences.zh: 洪謝曰：「不忍負朱公。」

translations.literal: Hong apologized, saying: "I could not bear to betray Lord Zhu."
translations.idiomatic: Hong bowed and said, "I could not bring myself to betray Lord Zhu."

sentences.zh: 與延祚皆斬揚州市。

translations.literal: He and Yanzuo were both executed in the Yangzhou marketplace.
translations.idiomatic: He and Yanzuo were both beheaded in the Yangzhou marketplace.

sentences.zh: 以劉存守鄂州。

translations.literal: Liu Cun was appointed to guard Ezhou.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Cun was left to garrison Ezhou.

sentences.zh: 行密死，馬殷遂取其地。

translations.literal: When Xingmi died, Ma Yin then took those territories.
translations.idiomatic: After Yang Xingmi's death, Ma Yin seized those territories.

sentences.zh: 鍾傳，洪州高安人。

translations.literal: Zhong Chuan was a man of Gao'an in Hongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong Chuan was a native of Gao'an in Hongzhou.

sentences.zh: 以負販自業，或勸其為盜必大顯。

translations.literal: He made his living as a peddler; some urged him that if he became a bandit he would surely achieve great renown.
translations.idiomatic: He made his living as a peddler until someone told him that if he turned to banditry he would surely rise to greatness.

sentences.zh: 時王仙芝猖狂，江南大亂，眾推傳為長，乃鳩夷獠，依山為壁，至萬人，自稱高安鎮撫使。

translations.literal: When Wang Xianzhi ran rampant and Jiangnan fell into great disorder, the crowd pressed Chuan as leader; he then gathered Yi and Liao tribesmen, relied on the mountains as ramparts, reached ten thousand men, and styled himself Pacification Commissioner of Gao'an.
translations.idiomatic: While Wang Xianzhi ravaged the south and Jiangnan fell into chaos, the people acclaimed Chuan as their leader. He gathered Yi and Liao tribesmen, fortified the mountains, and mustered ten thousand men, styling himself Pacification Commissioner of Gao'an.

sentences.zh: 仙芝遣柳彥璋略撫州，不能守，傳入據之，言諸朝，詔即拜刺史。

translations.literal: Xianzhi sent Liu Yanzhang to seize Fuzhou but he could not hold it; Chuan entered and occupied it, reported to the court, and an edict at once appointed him prefect.
translations.idiomatic: Xianzhi sent Liu Yanzhang against Fuzhou, but Yanzhang could not hold it. Chuan entered and seized the city, petitioned the court, and was immediately confirmed as prefect.

sentences.zh: 中和二年，逐江西觀察使高茂卿，遂有洪州。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhonghe he drove out Jiangxi observation commissioner Gao Maoqing and thereby possessed Hongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Zhonghe he drove out the Jiangxi observation commissioner Gao Maoqing and took Hongzhou.

sentences.zh: 撫民危全諷間傳之去，竊州以叛，使弟仔昌據信州。

translations.literal: The Fuzhou native Wei Quanfeng, taking advantage of Chuan's absence, stole the prefecture in rebellion and had his younger brother Zichang hold Xinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Quanfeng of Fuzhou, while Chuan was away, seized the prefecture in revolt and posted his younger brother Zichang at Xinzhou.

sentences.zh: 僖宗擢傳江西團練使，俄拜鎮南節度使、檢校太保、中書令，爵潁川郡王，又徙南平。

translations.literal: Emperor Xizong promoted Chuan to Jiangxi training commissioner; shortly he was appointed Zhennan military governor, acting Grand Guardian, Director of the Secretariat, enfeoffed as Prince of Yingchuan Commandery, and later transferred to Nanping.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xizong appointed him Jiangxi training commissioner, then shortly confirmed him as Zhennan military governor, acting Grand Guardian, Director of the Secretariat, and Prince of Yingchuan Commandery, later transferring his commission to Nanping.

sentences.zh: 傳率兵圍撫州，天火其城，士民讙驚，諸將請急攻之，傳曰：「乘人之險，不可。」

translations.literal: Chuan led troops to besiege Fuzhou; heaven set fire to its walls; soldiers and civilians were thrown into alarm; the generals asked to attack at once; Chuan said: "To take advantage of another's peril is not permissible.
translations.idiomatic: Chuan besieged Fuzhou. Heaven-sent fire broke out in the city, throwing soldiers and civilians into panic. His generals urged an immediate assault, but Chuan said, "We must not profit from another's calamity.

sentences.zh: 乃祝曰：「全諷罪，無害民者。」

translations.literal: He then prayed: "Let Quanfeng alone be guilty; let no harm come to the people."
translations.idiomatic: He prayed aloud, "Let Quanfeng alone bear the guilt; let no harm come to the people."

sentences.zh: 火即止。

translations.literal: The fire then ceased.
translations.idiomatic: The fire died away.

sentences.zh: 全諷聞，謝罪聽命，以女女傳子匡時。

translations.literal: Quanfeng heard of it, apologized and submitted to orders, and gave his daughter in marriage to Chuan's son Kuangshi.
translations.idiomatic: Quanfeng heard of this, submitted in apology, and gave his daughter in marriage to Chuan's son Kuangshi.

sentences.zh: 傳以匡時為袁州刺史，擊馬殷。

translations.literal: Chuan made Kuangshi prefect of Yuanzhou and attacked Ma Yin.
translations.idiomatic: Chuan appointed Kuangshi prefect of Yuanzhou and sent him against Ma Yin.

sentences.zh: 又以彭玕為吉州刺史。

translations.literal: He also made Peng Gan prefect of Jizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He also appointed Peng Gan prefect of Jizhou.

sentences.zh: 玕，健將也，傳倚以為重。

translations.literal: Gan was a stalwart general; Chuan relied on him as a weighty asset.
translations.idiomatic: Peng Gan was a formidable commander on whom Chuan relied heavily.

sentences.zh: 廣明後，州縣不鄉貢，惟傳歲薦士，行鄉飲酒禮，率官屬臨觀，資以裝賫，故士不遠千里走傳府。

translations.literal: After Guangming, prefectures and counties did not present candidates for the provincial examinations; only Chuan annually recommended scholars, performed the district drinking ceremony, led his officials to attend and observe, and supplied travel expenses—therefore scholars did not hesitate to travel a thousand li to Chuan's headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: After the Guangming era, most prefectures ceased sending examination candidates, but Chuan alone continued to recommend scholars each year, held the district drinking ceremony, led his officials in attendance, and provided travel funds. Scholars came from a thousand li away to seek his patronage.

sentences.zh: 傳少射獵，醉遇虎，與鬥，虎搏其肩，而傳亦持虎不置，會人斬虎，然後免。

translations.literal: In youth Chuan hunted with bow; drunk he met a tiger and fought it; the tiger struck his shoulder, yet Chuan also held the tiger and would not release it; by chance someone cut down the tiger, and only then was he spared.
translations.idiomatic: In his youth Chuan was a hunter. Once, drunk, he met a tiger and grappled with it. The beast clawed his shoulder, but Chuan would not let go until bystanders killed the tiger and he was freed.

sentences.zh: 既貴，悔之，戒諸子曰：「士處世，尚智與謀，勿效吾暴虎也。」

translations.literal: Once he had risen high he regretted it and admonished his sons: "A gentleman in the world esteems wisdom and stratagem—do not imitate my fighting a tiger bare-handed.
translations.idiomatic: After he rose to power he regretted the episode and warned his sons, "A gentleman in this world must prize wit and strategy. Do not imitate my foolhardy bout with a tiger.

sentences.zh: 乃畫搏虎狀以示子孫。

translations.literal: He then painted the scene of fighting the tiger to show his descendants.
translations.idiomatic: He had the scene painted as a warning to his descendants.

sentences.zh: 凡出軍攻戰，必禱佛祠，積餌餅為犀象，高數尋。

translations.literal: Whenever he marched out to attack in battle he always prayed at Buddhist shrines, piling cakes into rhinoceroses and elephants several zhang high.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he took the field he prayed at Buddhist shrines and piled cakes into rhinoceros and elephant figures several yards high.

sentences.zh: 晚節重斂，商人至棄其貨去。

translations.literal: In his later years he taxed heavily; merchants even abandoned their goods and left.
translations.idiomatic: In his later years he taxed heavily, and merchants sometimes abandoned their goods rather than pay.

sentences.zh: 天祐三年卒。

translations.literal: He died in the third year of Tianyou.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the third year of Tianyou.

sentences.zh: 匡時自立為節度觀察留後。

translations.literal: Kuangshi installed himself as acting military governor and observation commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Kuangshi proclaimed himself acting military governor and observation commissioner.

sentences.zh: 次子匡範為江州刺史，怨兄立，挈州附淮南，因言兄結汴人圖揚州。

translations.literal: His second son Kuangfan was prefect of Jiangzhou; resenting his elder brother's elevation, he brought the prefecture over to Huainan and reported that his brother had joined with Bian men to plot against Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: His second son Kuangfan, prefect of Jiangzhou, resented his brother's succession. He surrendered his prefecture to Huainan and claimed that his brother was conspiring with the Bian faction against Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 楊渥使秦裴攻匡時，圍洪州。

translations.literal: Yang Wo sent Qin Pei to attack Kuangshi and besieged Hongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Wo sent Qin Pei against Kuangshi and laid siege to Hongzhou.

sentences.zh: 匡時城守不出，凡三月，城陷，淮軍大掠三日止，執匡時及司馬陳象歸揚州。

translations.literal: Kuangshi defended the city and would not come out; in all three months the city fell; the Huainan army plundered greatly for three days before stopping; they seized Kuangshi and Chief Administrator Chen Xiang and returned to Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Kuangshi held the city for three months without sallying forth. When it fell, the Huainan army plundered for three days before stopping. Kuangshi and Chief Administrator Chen Xiang were taken to Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 渥切責，匡時頓首請死，渥哀赦之，斬象於市。

translations.literal: Wo sharply reproached him; Kuangshi kowtowed and begged for death; Wo pitied and pardoned him, and executed Xiang in the marketplace.
translations.idiomatic: Wo rebuked him sharply. Kuangshi kowtowed and begged for death. Wo took pity and spared him, but Chen Xiang was beheaded in the marketplace.

sentences.zh: 彭玕既失援，厚結馬殷，且觀虛實，使者還曰：「殷將校輯睦，未可圖也。」

translations.literal: Peng Gan, having lost support, bound himself closely to Ma Yin and also observed the true situation; the envoy returned saying: "Yin's officers and generals are harmonious—he cannot be plotted against.
translations.idiomatic: Having lost his patron, Peng Gan cultivated Ma Yin and sent envoys to probe his strength. They returned saying, "Yin's commanders are united in purpose—he cannot be overthrown.

sentences.zh: 遂歸款。

translations.literal: He then submitted in allegiance.
translations.idiomatic: He then submitted in allegiance.

sentences.zh: 玕通《左氏春秋》，嘗募求西京《石經》，厚賜以金。

translations.literal: Gan was versed in the Zuo Commentary to the Spring and Autumn Annals; he once recruited seekers of the Western Capital Stone Classics and richly rewarded them with gold.
translations.idiomatic: Peng Gan was versed in the Zuo Commentary. He once offered lavish rewards in gold to anyone who could procure copies of the Western Capital Stone Classics.

sentences.zh: 揚州人至相語曰：「十金易一筆，百金償一篇，況得士乎？」

translations.literal: People in Yangzhou said to one another: "Ten in gold for one brushstroke, a hundred in gold for one essay—how much more to obtain a scholar?
translations.idiomatic: People in Yangzhou remarked to one another, "Ten ounces of gold for a single brushstroke, a hundred for an essay—what would it cost to win a true scholar?

sentences.zh: 故士人多往依之。

translations.literal: Therefore many scholars went to rely on him.
translations.idiomatic: For this reason many scholars flocked to his service.

sentences.zh: 始，危全諷聞匡時立，喜曰：「聽鍾郎為節度三年，我自取之。」

translations.literal: At first, when Wei Quanfeng heard that Kuangshi had been installed, he rejoiced and said: "Let Master Zhong be military governor for three years—I will take it myself.
translations.idiomatic: When Wei Quanfeng first heard that Kuangshi had succeeded, he rejoiced and said, "Let Master Zhong hold the commission for three years—I will take it myself then.

sentences.zh: 及渥兵盛，不敢救，潛謀攻渥。

translations.literal: When Wo's troops grew strong he dared not rescue him and secretly plotted to attack Wo.
translations.idiomatic: But when Yang Wo's army grew powerful, Quanfeng dared not intervene and secretly plotted against him.

sentences.zh: 會淮南亡將王茂章過州，請曰：「聞公欲大舉，願見諸將軍才否。」

translations.literal: It happened that the Huainan fugitive general Wang Maozhang passed through the prefecture and requested: "I hear my lord wishes a great campaign—I wish to see whether your generals have talent.
translations.idiomatic: The Huainan fugitive general Wang Maozhang passed through and asked, "I hear you mean to mount a major campaign. May I see whether your generals are up to it?

sentences.zh: 全諷搜眾十萬，邀茂章觀之，對曰：「揚州有士三等，公眾正當其下，盍更益之？」

translations.literal: Quanfeng mustered a host of a hundred thousand and invited Maozhang to observe them; he replied: "Yangzhou has troops of three grades—my lord's host ranks only at the lowest; why not increase them further?"
translations.idiomatic: Quanfeng mustered a host of a hundred thousand and invited Maozhang to review them. Maozhang replied, "Yangzhou fields troops of three grades. Yours ranks only at the lowest. Why not raise more?"

sentences.zh: 全諷不能答。

translations.literal: Quanfeng could not answer.
translations.idiomatic: Quanfeng had no reply.

sentences.zh: 後為楊氏所並。

translations.literal: Later he was annexed by the Yang clan.
translations.idiomatic: He was later absorbed by the Yang clan.

sentences.zh: 劉漢宏

translations.literal: Liu Hanhong
translations.idiomatic: Liu Hanhong

sentences.zh: 劉漢宏，本兗州小史，從大將擊王仙芝，劫輜重叛去。

translations.literal: Liu Hanhong was originally a petty clerk of Yanzhou; he followed a great general to attack Wang Xianzhi, plundered the baggage train, and rebelled and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Hanhong had begun as a petty clerk in Yanzhou. While campaigning against Wang Xianzhi under a senior commander, he looted the baggage train and deserted.

sentences.zh: 乾符末，略江陵，焚民室廬，廛無完家。

translations.literal: At the end of Qianfu he overran Jiangling, burned the people's houses and huts, and not a single marketplace household remained intact.
translations.idiomatic: At the close of the Qianfu era he overran Jiangling, burned dwellings throughout the city, and left not one household intact in the markets.

sentences.zh: 於是都統王鐸遣將崔鍇降之，表為宿州刺史，漢宏恨賞薄，有望言。

translations.literal: Thereupon overall commander Wang Duo sent the general Cui Kai to accept his surrender and memorialized to appoint him prefect of Suzhou; Hanhong resented the meager reward and spoke words of ambition.
translations.idiomatic: The overall commander Wang Duo sent Cui Kai to accept his surrender and secured his appointment as prefect of Suzhou. Hanhong resented the meager reward and began to speak openly of greater ambitions.

sentences.zh: 會浙東觀察使柳瑫得罪，乃授漢宏觀察使，代之。

translations.literal: It happened that Zhedong observation commissioner Liu Tang offended and was punished; Hanhong was then appointed observation commissioner in his place.
translations.idiomatic: When the Zhedong observation commissioner Liu Tang fell from favor, Hanhong was appointed observation commissioner in his stead.

sentences.zh: 僖宗在蜀，貢輸踵驛而西，帝悅，寵其軍為義勝軍，即授節度使。

translations.literal: Emperor Xizong was in Shu; tribute arrived in relays by post road westward; the emperor was pleased, favored his army as the Yisheng Army, and at once appointed him military governor.
translations.idiomatic: With Emperor Xizong in exile in Shu, Hanhong's tribute arrived in an unbroken stream along the post roads. The emperor was pleased, renamed his force the Yisheng Army, and confirmed him as military governor.

sentences.zh: 漢宏既有七州，誌侈大，輒曰：「天下方亂，卯金刀非吾尚誰哉？」

translations.literal: Once Hanhong possessed seven prefectures his ambitions grew extravagant; he would say: "The realm is in disorder—if not I for the Liu surname, then who?
translations.idiomatic: Once he held seven prefectures his ambitions swelled, and he would say, "The realm is in chaos—if the Liu throne is not for me, then for whom?

sentences.zh: 鴉噪諸廷，命斫樹，或曰：「巨木不可伐。」

translations.literal: Crows cawed throughout the halls; he ordered the trees cut down; someone said: "Great trees cannot be felled."
translations.idiomatic: Crows clamored throughout his halls, and he ordered the trees cut down. An adviser said, "Great trees cannot be felled so easily."

sentences.zh: 怒曰：「吾能斬白蛇，何畏一木！」

translations.literal: In anger he said: "I can cut down the white serpent—why fear a single tree!"
translations.idiomatic: He raged, "I slew the white serpent—why should I fear one tree!"

sentences.zh: 中和二年，遣弟漢宥率諸將攻杭州，壁西陵，為董昌所敗。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhonghe he sent his younger brother Hanyou leading the generals to attack Hangzhou, encamped at Xiling, and was defeated by Dong Chang.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Zhonghe he sent his brother Hanyou with his generals against Hangzhou. They encamped at Xiling and were defeated by Dong Chang.

sentences.zh: 復遣兵七萬瀕江而屯，昌使錢镠宵濟襲破之。

translations.literal: He again sent seventy thousand troops to camp along the river; Chang had Qian Liu cross by night and raid and defeat them.
translations.idiomatic: He sent seventy thousand men to camp along the river. Chang dispatched Qian Liu, who crossed by night and routed them.

sentences.zh: 明年，漢宏屯黃嶺，發洞獠同攻昌，镠出富陽擊諸營，多潰去。

translations.literal: The next year Hanhong encamped at Huangling, mobilized cave tribes and Liao to attack Chang together; Liu marched out from Fuyang and struck the various camps; many collapsed and fled.
translations.idiomatic: The following year Hanhong encamped at Huangling and mobilized cave tribes and Liao auxiliaries against Chang. Qian Liu marched from Fuyang, struck their camps, and put many to flight.

sentences.zh: 漢宏大沮，悉軍十萬，列艦西陵，謀宵濟襲昌。

translations.literal: Hanhong was greatly discouraged; he mustered the whole army of a hundred thousand, arrayed warships at Xiling, and planned to cross by night and surprise Chang.
translations.idiomatic: Deeply discouraged, Hanhong mustered his entire force of a hundred thousand, lined his ships at Xiling, and planned a night crossing to surprise Chang.

sentences.zh: 禱於江，有一矢墜前，惡之。

translations.literal: He prayed at the river; an arrow fell before him; he regarded it as ill-omened.
translations.idiomatic: He prayed at the riverbank. An arrow fell before him, which he took as an ill omen.

sentences.zh: 俄與镠遇，镠俘馘五千，漢宏羸服走，或執之，紿而免。

translations.literal: Shortly he met Liu; Liu captured five thousand heads; Hanhong fled in tattered clothes; some seized him, but he deceived them and escaped.
translations.idiomatic: He soon met Qian Liu in battle. Liu took five thousand heads. Hanhong fled in rags. He was once seized but talked his way free.

sentences.zh: 明日復戰，镠斬其弟漢容、將辛約。

translations.literal: The next day they fought again; Liu beheaded his younger brother Hanrong and the general Xin Yue.
translations.idiomatic: They fought again the next day. Liu beheaded Hanhong's brother Hanrong and the general Xin Yue.

sentences.zh: 時鍾季文守明州，盧約處州，蔣瑰婺州，杜雄臺州，朱褒溫州。

translations.literal: At this time Zhong Jiwen held Mingzhou, Lu Yue held Chuzhou, Jiang Gui held Wuzhou, Du Xiong held Taizhou, and Zhu Bao held Wenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong Jiwen held Mingzhou, Lu Yue Chuzhou, Jiang Gui Wuzhou, Du Xiong Taizhou, and Zhu Bao Wenzhou.

sentences.zh: 褒兵最強，故漢宏使褒治大艦習戰，以史惠、施堅實、韓公汶將其軍。

translations.literal: Bao's troops were strongest; therefore Hanhong had Bao build great warships and drill for battle, with Shi Hui, Shi Jianshi, and Han Gongwen commanding his army.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Bao's force was the strongest, so Hanhong had him build great warships and drill for naval combat under Shi Hui, Shi Jianshi, and Han Gongwen.

sentences.zh: 帝聞杭、越挐戰，遣中人焦居璠持節詔通好，皆不奉詔。

translations.literal: The emperor heard that Hang and Yue were locked in combat; he sent the eunuch Jiao Jufan bearing credentials to order reconciliation; none obeyed the edict.
translations.idiomatic: Learning that Hang and Yue were locked in combat, the emperor sent the eunuch Jiao Jufan with credentials to command peace. Neither side obeyed.

sentences.zh: 光啟二年，镠率諸將攻越，自趨導山，破公汶於曹娥埭。

translations.literal: In the second year of Guangqi, Liu led the generals to attack Yue, himself pressing toward Daoshan, and defeated Gongwen at Cao'e Ford.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Guangqi, Qian Liu led his generals against Yue, advanced on Daoshan himself, and defeated Han Gongwen at Cao'e Ford.

sentences.zh: 與褒戰，燒其艦，進屯豐山。

translations.literal: He fought Bao, burned his ships, and advanced to encamp at Fengshan.
translations.idiomatic: He fought Zhu Bao, burned his fleet, and advanced to encamp at Fengshan.

sentences.zh: 堅實詣镠降，漢宏率麾下六百人走臺州，镠斬其母妻於屯。

translations.literal: Jianshi came to Liu to surrender; Hanhong led six hundred followers in flight to Taizhou; Liu beheaded his mother and wife at the camp.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Jianshi surrendered to Qian Liu. Hanhong fled to Taizhou with six hundred followers. Liu executed Hanhong's mother and wife at his camp.

sentences.zh: 杜雄饗其軍，皆醉，執漢宏以見董昌。

translations.literal: Du Xiong feasted his army; all were drunk; he seized Hanhong and presented him to Dong Chang.
translations.idiomatic: Du Xiong feasted Hanhong's troops until they were drunk, seized Hanhong, and brought him before Dong Chang.

sentences.zh: 漢宏曰：「自古豈有不亡國邪？」

translations.literal: Hanhong said: "Since antiquity has there ever been a state that did not perish?
translations.idiomatic: Hanhong said, "Since antiquity, has any state not perished in its time?

sentences.zh: 昌使斬於市，叱刑者曰：「吾節度使，非庸人可殺。

translations.literal: Chang had him executed in the marketplace and shouted at the executioner: "I am a military governor—not someone a common man may kill.
translations.idiomatic: Chang ordered his execution in the marketplace and shouted at the headsman, "I am a military governor—not some common felon you may kill.

sentences.zh: 我嘗夢持金殺我者，必錢镠也。」

translations.literal: I once dreamed that he who would kill me holding gold must be Qian Liu."
translations.idiomatic: I once dreamed that my killer would bear gold—it must be Qian Liu."

sentences.zh: 昌命镠斬之。

translations.literal: Chang ordered Liu to behead him.
translations.idiomatic: Chang ordered Qian Liu to behead him.

sentences.zh: 張雄，泗州漣水人。

translations.literal: Zhang Xiong was a man of Lianshui in Sizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Xiong was a native of Lianshui in Sizhou.

sentences.zh: 與里人馮弘鐸皆為武寧軍偏將。

translations.literal: He and his fellow townsman Feng Hongduo were both deputy generals of the Wuning Army.
translations.idiomatic: He and his fellow townsman Feng Hongduo both served as deputy generals in the Wuning Army.

sentences.zh: 弘鐸為吏辱，雄為辯數，並見疑於節度使時溥。

translations.literal: Hongduo was insulted by a clerk; Xiong argued on his behalf with eloquence; both came under suspicion by military governor Shi Pu.
translations.idiomatic: When Hongduo was insulted by a clerk, Xiong argued eloquently in his defense. Both men fell under suspicion with the military governor Shi Pu.

sentences.zh: 二人懼禍，乃合兵三百度江，壁白下，取蘇州據之。

translations.literal: The two men feared disaster; they combined three hundred troops, crossed the river, fortified Baixia, and took Suzhou and held it.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing for their lives, the two combined three hundred men, crossed the Yangzi, fortified Baixia, and seized Suzhou.

sentences.zh: 稍稍嘯會，戰艦千餘，兵五萬，乃自號「天成軍」。

translations.literal: Gradually they gathered followers; warships exceeded a thousand; troops reached fifty thousand; they then styled themselves the "Tiancheng Army."
translations.idiomatic: Their following grew steadily until they fielded more than a thousand warships and fifty thousand men, styling their force the Tiancheng Army.

sentences.zh: 鎮海節度使周寶之敗，奔常州，聞高駢將徐約兵銳甚，誘之使擊雄，與之蘇州。

translations.literal: When Zhenhai military governor Zhou Bao was defeated he fled to Changzhou; hearing that Gao Pian's general Xu Yue's troops were very sharp, he enticed him to attack Xiong and offered him Suzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When the Zhenhai military governor Zhou Bao was defeated, he fled to Changzhou. Hearing that Xu Yue, a general of Gao Pian, commanded a formidable force, he lured him against Zhang Xiong with the promise of Suzhou.

sentences.zh: 雄匿眾海中，使別將趙暉據上元，資以舟械。

translations.literal: Xiong hid his host on the sea and sent the subordinate general Zhao Hui to hold Shangyuan, supplying him with boats and weapons.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Xiong kept his main force at sea and posted Zhao Hui at Shangyuan with ships and arms.

sentences.zh: 寶兵散，多降暉，眾數萬。

translations.literal: Bao's troops scattered; many surrendered to Hui; his host numbered tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Bao's army broke apart, and many of his men surrendered to Zhao Hui, whose force soon numbered in the tens of thousands.

sentences.zh: 雄即以上元為西州。

translations.literal: Xiong then made Shangyuan his western prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Xiong made Shangyuan his western capital.

sentences.zh: 負其才，欲治臺城為府，旌旗衣服僭王者。

translations.literal: Relying on his talent, he wished to govern Taicheng as his headquarters; banners, flags, and garments usurped those of kings.
translations.idiomatic: Confident in his abilities, he meant to make Taicheng his seat of government, and his banners, regalia, and dress all aped royal style.

sentences.zh: 楊行密圍揚州，畢師鐸厚賫寶幣，啖雄連和。

translations.literal: Yang Xingmi besieged Yangzhou; Bi Shiduo richly bestowed treasure and currency to entice Xiong into alliance.
translations.idiomatic: While Yang Xingmi besieged Yangzhou, Bi Shiduo lavished treasure on Zhang Xiong to win an alliance.

sentences.zh: 雄率軍浮海屯東塘。

translations.literal: Xiong led his army by sea to encamp at Dongtang.
translations.idiomatic: Xiong led his fleet to Dongtang by sea.

sentences.zh: 是時揚州圍久，皮囊革帶食無余，軍中殺人代糧，才千錢。

translations.literal: At this time the siege of Yangzhou had lasted long; leather bags and belts were eaten with nothing left; in the army men were killed for rations at only a thousand cash apiece.
translations.idiomatic: The siege of Yangzhou had dragged on so long that soldiers ate leather bags and belts until nothing remained. Human flesh sold for a thousand cash in the camp.

sentences.zh: 聞雄至，間道挾珍走軍，以銀二斤易斗米，逮糠乞以差為直。

translations.literal: Hearing Xiong had arrived, they took secret routes bearing treasures to his army; two catties of silver bought a dou of rice; even bran was begged for at graded prices.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing that Xiong had arrived, they slipped out by hidden routes with treasures to his camp. Two catties of silver bought a single dou of rice; even bran was traded at graded prices.

sentences.zh: 雄軍富過所欲，即不戰去。

translations.literal: Xiong's army grew richer than they desired and at once departed without fighting.
translations.idiomatic: Xiong's army grew wealthier than it could use and withdrew without fighting.

sentences.zh: 暉數剽江道，雄擊殺之，坑其眾，自屯上元。

translations.literal: Hui repeatedly raided the river routes; Xiong attacked and killed him, buried his host alive, and himself encamped at Shangyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Hui had repeatedly raided the river routes. Xiong killed him, buried his troops alive, and returned to garrison Shangyuan.

sentences.zh: 大順初，以上元為升州，詔授雄刺史。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Dashun, Shangyuan was made Shengzhou; an edict appointed Xiong prefect.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Dashun, Shangyuan was renamed Shengzhou, and an edict confirmed Xiong as prefect.

sentences.zh: 未幾，卒。

translations.literal: Before long he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died soon afterward.

sentences.zh: 雄善馭眾，人思之，為立廟。

translations.literal: Xiong was skilled at controlling the multitude; people missed him and erected a shrine.
translations.idiomatic: Xiong was skilled at commanding men, and the people missed him so deeply that they built him a shrine.

sentences.zh: 弘鐸代為刺史。

translations.literal: Hongduo succeeded him as prefect.
translations.idiomatic: Hongduo succeeded him as prefect.

sentences.zh: 弘鐸善騎射，侃侃若儒者。

translations.literal: Hongduo was skilled in horsemanship and archery, and spoke with ease like a Confucian scholar.
translations.idiomatic: Hongduo was an expert horseman and archer who spoke with the easy grace of a scholar.

sentences.zh: 行密已得淮南，弘鐸納好。

translations.literal: Xingmi had already obtained Huainan; Hongduo entered into friendly relations.
translations.idiomatic: Once Yang Xingmi held Huainan, Hongduo sought friendly ties with him.

sentences.zh: 然倚兵艦完利，謀取潤州，遣客尚公乃進說行密，行密不從。

translations.literal: Yet relying on his complete and sharp warships and troops, he plotted to seize Runzhou; he sent the guest Shang Gongnai to advance persuasion to Xingmi, but Xingmi would not follow.
translations.idiomatic: Yet relying on his powerful fleet, he plotted to seize Runzhou and sent his adviser Shang Gongnai to persuade Yang Xingmi, who refused.

sentences.zh: 客曰：「公不見聽，未知勝幾樓船？」

translations.literal: The guest said: "If my lord will not heed, who knows how many tower-ships will win?
translations.idiomatic: The envoy said, "If you will not listen, how many of your tower-ships do you think will survive?

sentences.zh: 時行密大將田頵在宣州，陰圖弘鐸，募工治艦。

translations.literal: At this time Xingmi's great general Tian Jun was at Xuanzhou, secretly plotting against Hongduo, recruiting craftsmen to build warships.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Xingmi's great general Tian Jun was then at Xuanzhou, secretly plotting against Hongduo and recruiting shipwrights.

sentences.zh: 工曰：「上元為舟，市木遠方，堅致可勝數十歲。」

translations.literal: The craftsmen said: "At Shangyuan for building ships, timber is bought from distant places, firm and durable enough to last several decades.
translations.idiomatic: The shipwrights said, "At Shangyuan they buy timber from far away—timber so sound it lasts decades.

sentences.zh: 頵曰：「我為舟於一用，不計其久，取木於境可也。」

translations.literal: Jun said: "I build ships for a single use and do not reckon on their lasting—taking timber within the borders will suffice."
translations.idiomatic: Jun replied, "I build ships for a single campaign, not for the ages. Local timber will do."

sentences.zh: 弘鐸介宣、揚間，不自安，而州數有怪。

translations.literal: Hongduo stood between Xuan and Yang and was ill at ease; moreover the prefecture repeatedly had strange occurrences.
translations.idiomatic: Caught between Xuanzhou and Yangzhou, Hongduo grew uneasy, and strange omens multiplied in his prefecture.

sentences.zh: 天復二年，大風發屋，巨木飛舞，州人駭曰：「州且易主。」

translations.literal: In the second year of Tianfu a great wind tore up houses and sent huge trees flying; the people of the prefecture were alarmed and said: "The prefecture is about to change masters.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Tianfu a violent wind tore houses apart and sent great trees flying. The people cried in alarm, "The prefecture is about to change hands!

sentences.zh: 大將馮暉等勸弘鐸悉軍南向，聲言討鍾傳，實襲頵。

translations.literal: The great generals Feng Hui and others urged Hongduo to lead the whole army south, proclaiming an attack on Zhong Chuan while in fact striking Jun.
translations.idiomatic: His generals Feng Hui and others urged him to march south with his entire force, claiming an expedition against Zhong Chuan while actually striking Tian Jun.

sentences.zh: 行密知之，遣客說止，不聽。

translations.literal: Xingmi learned of it and sent a guest to persuade him to stop; he would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Xingmi learned of the plan and sent an envoy to dissuade him, but Hongduo would not listen.

sentences.zh: 頵逆擊於曷山，弘鐸大敗，收殘士欲入海。

translations.literal: Jun met him in counterattack at Yeshan; Hongduo was greatly defeated, gathered his remnant troops, and wished to flee to sea.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Jun met him at Yeshan and routed him utterly. Hongduo gathered his shattered remnants and prepared to flee by sea.

sentences.zh: 行密懼復振，遣人迎犒東塘，好謂曰：「兵有勝負，今眾尚強，乃自棄於海，奈何？

translations.literal: Xingmi feared he would revive; he sent men to welcome and feast him at Dongtang, speaking kindly: "Armies have victory and defeat—your host is still strong; why abandon yourselves to the sea?
translations.idiomatic: Fearing Hongduo might recover, Yang Xingmi sent men to welcome him at Dongtang with feasts and kind words: "Armies win and lose, but yours is still strong. Why throw yourselves into the sea?

sentences.zh: 吾府雖隘，尚可以居。

translations.literal: Though my headquarters is narrow, it can still serve to dwell in.
translations.idiomatic: My headquarters may be modest, but there is room for you.

sentences.zh: 若欲揚州，我且讓公。」

translations.literal: If you desire Yangzhou, I will yield it to my lord.
translations.idiomatic: If you want Yangzhou, I will yield it to you.

sentences.zh: 弘鐸舉軍盡哭。

translations.literal: Hongduo's whole army wept together.
translations.idiomatic: Hongduo's entire army wept together.

sentences.zh: 行密挐飛艫，不持兵入其軍，執弘鐸手尉勉，遂以歸，表為淮南節度副使。

translations.literal: Xingmi took swift warships, entered his army without bearing weapons, took Hongduo's hand and comforted him, then brought him back and memorialized to appoint him deputy military governor of Huainan.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Xingmi came in swift ships, entered the camp unarmed, took Hongduo's hand in consolation, and brought him home. He was memorialized as deputy military governor of Huainan.

sentences.zh: 見尚公乃曰：「頗憶為馮公求潤州否？

translations.literal: Seeing Shang Gongnai he said: "Do you still recall begging Runzhou for Lord Feng?
translations.idiomatic: Seeing Shang Gongnai, he said, "Do you still remember begging Runzhou on Feng's behalf?

sentences.zh: 何多尚邪？」

translations.literal: Why so much Shang?
translations.idiomatic: Why so much talk of Shang?

sentences.zh: 謝曰：「臣為君，恨其未遂。」

translations.literal: He apologized, saying: "Your servant acted for my lord and regrets that it was not accomplished."
translations.idiomatic: He bowed and said, "I served my lord and regret that I failed."

sentences.zh: 行密笑曰：「吾得君，尚何憂？」

translations.literal: Xingmi laughed and said: "Having obtained you, what is there still to worry about?"
translations.idiomatic: Yang Xingmi laughed and said, "With you at my side, what have I to fear?"

sentences.zh: 徐約者，曹州人。

translations.literal: Xu Yue was a man of Caozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Yue was a native of Caozhou.

sentences.zh: 已得蘇州，有詔授刺史。

translations.literal: Having already obtained Suzhou, an edict appointed him prefect.
translations.idiomatic: Having seized Suzhou, he received an edict appointing him prefect.

sentences.zh: 錢镠遣弟銶攻之，約驅民墨镵其耏曰：「願戰南都。」

translations.literal: Qian Liu sent his younger brother Qian to attack him; Yue drove the people to tattoo their foreheads in ink, saying: "We wish to fight the Southern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: Qian Liu sent his brother Qian against him. Yue had the people tattoo their foreheads in ink with the words, "We will fight the Southern Capital.

sentences.zh: 從事或曰：「都者，國稱，杭終有國乎？」

translations.literal: A staff member said: "'Capital' is the designation of a state—will Hangzhou in the end have a kingdom?"
translations.idiomatic: A staff officer objected, "'Capital' is the title of a realm—does Hangzhou mean to proclaim a kingdom?"

sentences.zh: 約後浸窘，與其下哭而別，入海死。

translations.literal: Later Yue grew increasingly distressed; he wept in parting with his subordinates and died by entering the sea.
translations.idiomatic: Yue's situation grew desperate. He wept farewell to his followers and drowned himself at sea.

sentences.zh: 镠使沈粲守蘇州。

translations.literal: Liu had Shen Can guard Suzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Qian Liu appointed Shen Can to garrison Suzhou.

sentences.zh: 約眾降潤州阮結，結不能定。

translations.literal: Yue's host surrendered to Runzhou's Ruan Jie; Jie could not settle them.
translations.idiomatic: Yue's followers surrendered to Ruan Jie of Runzhou, who could not control them.

sentences.zh: 镠以成及討之，盡殲其眾。

translations.literal: Liu sent Cheng Ji to attack them and annihilated the host completely.
translations.idiomatic: Qian Liu sent Cheng Ji against them and annihilated them to the last man.

sentences.zh: 王潮，字信臣，光州固始人。

translations.literal: Wang Chao, style Xinchen, was a man of Gushi in Guangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Chao, styled Xinchen, was a native of Gushi in Guangzhou.

sentences.zh: 五代祖曄為固始令，民愛其仁，留之，因家焉。

translations.literal: His fifth-generation ancestor Ye was magistrate of Gushi; the people loved his benevolence and kept him there, and the family settled there.
translations.idiomatic: His fifth-generation ancestor Ye had served as magistrate of Gushi. The people loved his benevolence and persuaded him to stay, and the family settled there.

sentences.zh: 世以貲顯。

translations.literal: For generations they were prominent through wealth.
translations.idiomatic: For generations the family had grown prominent through wealth.

sentences.zh: 僖宗入蜀，盜興江、淮，壽春亡命王緒、劉行全合群盜據壽州。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xizong entered Shu, bandits rose on the Jiang and Huai; the Shouchun fugitives Wang Xu and Liu Xingquan combined bandit groups and seized Shouzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xizong fled to Shu, banditry flared along the Yangzi and Huai. The Shouchun outlaws Wang Xu and Liu Xingquan united bandit bands and seized Shouzhou.

sentences.zh: 未幾，眾萬餘，自稱將軍，復取光州，劫豪傑置軍中，潮自縣史署軍正，主稟庾，士推其信。
