translations.literal: Before long their host exceeded ten thousand; he styled himself general; he again took Guangzhou; he seized powerful men and placed them in the army; Chao from county clerk was appointed army steward, in charge of granaries, and the soldiers praised his trustworthiness.
translations.idiomatic: Before long their force exceeded ten thousand. Xu styled himself general, retook Guangzhou, and impressed local strongmen into his ranks. Chao, formerly a county clerk, was made army steward in charge of supplies, and the troops praised his reliability.

sentences.zh: 緒提二州籍附秦宗權。

translations.literal: Xu brought the registers of two prefectures and submitted to Qin Zongquan.
translations.idiomatic: Xu submitted the registers of two prefectures and attached himself to Qin Zongquan.

sentences.zh: 它日，賦不如期，宗權切責，緒懼，與行全拔眾南走，略潯陽、贛水，取汀州，自稱刺史，入漳州，皆不能有也。

translations.literal: Another day the tribute was not delivered on time; Zongquan sharply reproached him; Xu was afraid; with Xingquan he led the host south, overran Xunyang and the Gan River, took Tingzhou and styled himself prefect, entered Zhangzhou—yet could hold none of them.
translations.idiomatic: When tribute fell due and was not delivered, Zongquan rebuked him harshly. Xu fled south with Xingquan, overran Xunyang and the Gan valley, seized Tingzhou and styled himself prefect, and entered Zhangzhou—but could hold none of these places.

sentences.zh: 初以糧少，故兼道馳，約軍中曰：「以老孺從者斬！」

translations.literal: At first because grain was scarce they marched by combined routes at speed; he stipulated to the army: "Whoever is followed by the old or infants shall be beheaded!
translations.idiomatic: Grain was scarce, so they marched at forced pace. Xu ordered the army: "Anyone who brings the old or children along will be beheaded!

sentences.zh: 潮與弟審邽、審知奉母以行，緒切責潮曰：「吾聞軍行有法，無不法之軍。」

translations.literal: Chao with his younger brothers Shenbian and Shenzhi supported their mother on the march; Xu sharply reproached Chao: "I have heard that armies on campaign have laws—there is no army without law."
translations.idiomatic: Chao marched with his brothers Shenbian and Shenzhi, supporting their mother. Xu rebuked him sharply: "Armies on campaign have laws. No army is above the law."

sentences.zh: 對曰：「人皆有母，不聞有無母之人。」

translations.literal: He replied: "All men have mothers—I have never heard of men without mothers."
translations.idiomatic: Chao answered, "Every man has a mother. I have never heard of a man without one."

sentences.zh: 緒怒，欲斬其母，三子同辭曰：「事母猶事將軍也，殺其母焉用其子？」

translations.literal: Xu grew angry and wished to behead his mother; the three sons together said: "Serving one's mother is like serving the general—if you kill their mother, of what use are the sons?"
translations.idiomatic: Xu flew into a rage and meant to execute their mother. The three brothers pleaded together: "Serving one's mother is like serving a commander. Kill our mother, and what use are we to you?"

sentences.zh: 緒赦之。

translations.literal: Xu pardoned them.
translations.idiomatic: Xu relented.

sentences.zh: 會毋死，不敢哭，夜殯道左。

translations.literal: It happened that their mother died; they dared not weep and at night laid her out for encoffining by the roadside.
translations.idiomatic: Their mother died on the march. They dared not weep openly and laid her out for burial by the roadside that night.

sentences.zh: 時望氣者言軍中當有暴興者，緒潛視魁梧雄才，皆以事誅之，眾懼。

translations.literal: At this time a diviner of qi said that in the army someone would rise violently to power; Xu secretly watched for tall and heroic talents and executed them all on pretexts; the host was afraid.
translations.idiomatic: A geomancer declared that someone in the army would rise to sudden greatness. Xu secretly marked out tall, formidable men and executed them on one pretext or another until the troops were terrified.

sentences.zh: 次南安，潮語行全曰：「子美須眉，才絕眾，吾不知子死所。」

translations.literal: When they reached Nan'an, Chao said to Xingquan: "You are handsome in beard and brow, your talent surpasses the multitude—I do not know where you will die.
translations.idiomatic: At Nan'an, Chao told Xingquan, "You are a striking figure, and your talent surpasses all others. I do not know where you will meet your end.

sentences.zh: 而行全怪寤，亦不自安，與左右數十人伏叢翳，狙縛緒以徇。

translations.literal: Xingquan awoke from a strange dream and was also ill at ease; with several dozen close followers he hid in thick brush, ambushed and bound Xu, and displayed him to the army.
translations.idiomatic: Xingquan woke from an uneasy dream and grew restless himself. With several dozen followers he hid in the brush, ambushed Xu, bound him, and paraded him before the army.

sentences.zh: 眾呼萬歲，推行全為將軍，辭曰：「我不及潮，請以為主。」

translations.literal: The host shouted ten thousand years of life; they pressed Xingquan to be general; he declined, saying: "I am not the equal of Chao—please make him leader.
translations.idiomatic: The troops shouted their acclaim and pressed Xingquan to lead them. He declined: "I am not Chao's equal. Make him your leader.

sentences.zh: 潮苦讓不克，乃除地剚劍祝曰：「拜而劍三動者，我以為主。」

translations.literal: Chao earnestly declined but could not prevail; he then cleared ground, planted a sword, and prayed: "Whoever bows and the sword moves three times, I will make leader."
translations.idiomatic: Chao refused repeatedly but could not prevail. He cleared a patch of ground, planted a sword, and prayed: "Whichever of us bows and the sword moves three times shall be leader."

sentences.zh: 至審知，劍躍於地，眾以為神，皆拜之。

translations.literal: When it came to Shenzhi, the sword leaped from the ground; the host regarded it as divine and all bowed to him.
translations.idiomatic: When Shenzhi bowed, the sword leaped from the earth. The troops took it as a divine sign and bowed to him.

sentences.zh: 審知讓潮，自為副。

translations.literal: Shenzhi yielded to Chao and made himself deputy.
translations.idiomatic: Shenzhi yielded to Chao and took the post of deputy.

sentences.zh: 緒嘆曰：「我不能殺是子，非天乎！」

translations.literal: Xu sighed and said: "I could not kill this son—is it not Heaven's will!
translations.idiomatic: Xu sighed, "I could not kill this man—is it not Heaven's will!

sentences.zh: 潮令於軍曰：「天子蒙難，今當出交、廣，入巴、蜀，以幹王室。」

translations.literal: Chao ordered the army: "The Son of Heaven suffers hardship; we should now go out through Jiao and Guang, enter Ba and Shu, and serve the royal house."
translations.idiomatic: Chao proclaimed to the army, "The Son of Heaven is in peril. We shall march through Jiaozhi and Guangzhou into Ba and Shu to serve the throne."

sentences.zh: 於是悉師將行，會泉州刺史廖彥若貪暴，聞潮治軍有法，故州人奉牛酒迎潮。

translations.literal: Thereupon he was about to lead the whole army on the march when it happened that Quanzhou prefect Liao Yanruo was greedy and cruel; hearing that Chao governed the army with method, the people of the former prefecture brought oxen and wine to welcome Chao.
translations.idiomatic: As he prepared to march, the Quanzhou prefect Liao Yanruo was ruling with greed and cruelty. Hearing that Chao disciplined his troops well, the people of Quanzhou came out with oxen and wine to welcome him.

sentences.zh: 乃圍城，歲餘克之，殺彥若，遂有其地。

translations.literal: He then besieged the city; after more than a year he took it, killed Yanruo, and thereby possessed the territory.
translations.idiomatic: He besieged the city for more than a year, took it, executed Yanruo, and seized the territory.

sentences.zh: 初，黃巢將竊有福州，王師不能下，建人陳巖率眾拔之，又逐觀察使鄭鎰，自領州，詔即授刺史。

translations.literal: At first Huang Chao's generals meant to seize Fuzhou; the imperial army could not take it; the Jian native Chen Yan led the host to capture it, also drove out observation commissioner Zheng Yi, took the prefecture himself, and an edict at once appointed him prefect.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Chao's generals had meant to seize Fuzhou, but the imperial army could not take it. Chen Yan of Jian led his forces to capture the city, drove out the observation commissioner Zheng Yi, and was confirmed as prefect by edict.

sentences.zh: 久之，巖卒，其婿範暉擁兵自稱留後。

translations.literal: After a long while Yan died; his son-in-law Fan Hui gathered troops and styled himself acting governor.
translations.idiomatic: In time Chen Yan died. His son-in-law Fan Hui gathered troops and proclaimed himself acting governor.

sentences.zh: 巖舊將多歸潮，言暉可取，潮乃遣從弟彥復將兵，審知監之，攻福州。

translations.literal: Yan's former generals mostly came over to Chao and said Hui could be taken; Chao then sent his cousin Yanfu to lead troops with Shenzhi supervising, to attack Fuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Many of Chen Yan's former officers joined Chao and assured him that Fan Hui could be taken. Chao sent his cousin Yanfu with Shenzhi as overseer to attack Fuzhou.

sentences.zh: 審知乘白馬履行陣，望者披靡，號「白馬將軍」。

translations.literal: Shenzhi rode a white horse and walked through the battle lines; those who saw him collapsed before him; he was called the "White Horse General."
translations.idiomatic: Shenzhi rode a white horse through the battle lines, and all who saw him gave way. He was styled the White Horse General.

sentences.zh: 暉守彌年不下，潮令曰：「兵盡益兵，將盡益將，兵將盡，則吾至矣。」

translations.literal: Hui defended for a full year without falling; Chao ordered: "When soldiers are exhausted, add soldiers; when generals are exhausted, add generals; when soldiers and generals are exhausted, then I shall arrive.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Hui held out for a year. Chao declared, "When our soldiers are spent, we shall send more soldiers. When our generals are spent, we shall send more generals. When both are spent, I shall come myself.

sentences.zh: 於是彥復急攻，暉亡入海，追斬之。

translations.literal: Thereupon Yanfu pressed the attack urgently; Hui fled to sea; they pursued and beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: Yanfu pressed the assault. Fan Hui fled to sea and was pursued and killed.

sentences.zh: 建、汀二州皆舉籍聽命，潮乃盡有五州地。

translations.literal: Jian and Ting both submitted their registers and obeyed orders; Chao then fully possessed the territory of five prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: Jian and Ting submitted to his authority, and Chao came to hold five prefectures in all.

sentences.zh: 昭宗假潮福建等州圍練使，俄遷觀察使。

translations.literal: Emperor Zhaozong provisionally appointed Chao training commissioner of Fujian and other prefectures; shortly he was transferred to observation commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Zhaozong appointed him acting training commissioner of Fujian, then shortly promoted him to observation commissioner.

sentences.zh: 乃作四門義學，還流亡，定賦斂，遣吏勸農，人皆安之。

translations.literal: He then established the Four Gates Academy for righteous learning, restored the displaced, fixed taxes and levies, sent officials to encourage agriculture, and the people all found peace.
translations.idiomatic: He founded the Four Gates Academy, recalled exiles, fixed taxes and levies, sent officials to encourage farming, and the people lived in peace.

sentences.zh: 乾寧中，寵福州為威武軍，即拜潮節度使、檢校尚書左僕射。

translations.literal: During Qianning, Fuzhou was favored as the Weiwu Army; Chao was at once appointed military governor and acting Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: During Qianning, Fuzhou was elevated as the Weiwu Army command, and Chao was appointed military governor and acting Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈司空。

translations.literal: He died and was posthumously awarded Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously awarded the title Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 潮病，以審知權節度，讓審邽，不許。

translations.literal: When Chao fell ill he had Shenzhi act as military governor by authority; he yielded to Shenbian, but this was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: When Chao fell ill, he entrusted military authority to Shenzhi and offered the post to Shenbian, but the offer was refused.

sentences.zh: 詔審知檢校刑部尚書、節度觀察留後。

translations.literal: An edict appointed Shenzhi acting Minister of Justice and acting military governor and observation commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: An edict appointed Shenzhi acting Minister of Justice and acting military governor and observation commissioner.

sentences.zh: 厚事朱全忠，全忠薦為節度使、同中書門下平章事。

translations.literal: He treated Zhu Quanzhong lavishly; Quanzhong recommended him as military governor and Associate Director of the Secretariat with the Court.
translations.idiomatic: He cultivated Zhu Quanzhong lavishly, and Quanzhong secured his appointment as military governor and Associate Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 帝在鳳翔，賜審知朱詔，自三品皆得承制除授。

translations.literal: The emperor was at Fengxiang and bestowed on Shenzhi a vermilion edict: from the third rank downward he might appoint and dismiss by imperial commission.
translations.idiomatic: With the emperor at Fengxiang, Shenzhi received a vermilion edict empowering him to appoint and dismiss officials from the third rank downward on his own authority.

sentences.zh: 天祐初，進瑯邪郡王。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianyou he was advanced to Prince of Langye Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Tianyou he was enfeoffed as Prince of Langye Commandery.

sentences.zh: 審邽，字次都。

translations.literal: Shenbian, style Cidu.
translations.idiomatic: Shenbian, styled Cidu.

sentences.zh: 為泉州刺史，檢校司徒。

translations.literal: He was prefect of Quanzhou and acting Minister of Education.
translations.idiomatic: He served as prefect of Quanzhou and acting Minister of Education.

sentences.zh: 喜儒術，通《書》、《春秋》。

translations.literal: He delighted in Confucian learning and was versed in the Documents and the Spring and Autumn Annals.
translations.idiomatic: He delighted in Confucian learning and was versed in the Book of Documents and the Spring and Autumn Annals.

sentences.zh: 善吏治，流民還者假牛犁，興完廬舍。

translations.literal: He was skilled in governing through officials; to returning displaced persons he lent oxen and plows and raised and completed lodges and houses.
translations.idiomatic: He governed ably, lending oxen and plows to returning refugees and helping them rebuild their homes.

sentences.zh: 中原亂，公卿多來依之，振賦以財，如楊承休、鄭璘、韓偓、歸傳懿、楊贊圖、鄭戩等賴以免禍，審邽遣子延彬作招賢院以禮之。

translations.literal: When the Central Plains were in disorder, many ministers and nobles came to rely on him; he relieved them with wealth from taxes; such men as Yang Chenxiu, Zheng Lin, Han Wo, Gui Chuanyi, Yang Zantu, and Zheng Xian relied on this to escape calamity; Shenbian sent his son Yanbin to establish the Court for Recruiting the Worthy to honor them with ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: As the Central Plains fell into chaos, many court officials fled to him for refuge. He supported them from the treasury—men such as Yang Chenxiu, Zheng Lin, Han Wo, Gui Chuanyi, Yang Zantu, and Zheng Xian owed their survival to his patronage. Shenbian had his son Yanbin establish the Hall for Recruiting Talent to receive them with full ceremony.

sentences.zh: 劉知謙

translations.literal: Liu Zhiqian
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zhiqian

sentences.zh: 劉知謙，壽州上蔡人。

translations.literal: Liu Zhiqian was a man of Shangcai in Shouzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zhiqian was a native of Shangcai in Shouzhou.

sentences.zh: 避亂客封州，為清海牙將。

translations.literal: Fleeing disorder he sojourned at Fengzhou as a junior officer of Qinghai.
translations.idiomatic: Fleeing the chaos, he took refuge at Fengzhou as a junior officer under the Qinghai command.

sentences.zh: 節度使韋宙以兄女妻之，眾謂不可，宙曰：「若人狀貌非常，吾以子孫托之。」

translations.literal: Military governor Wei Zhou gave him his elder brother's daughter in marriage; the crowd said it was not permissible; Zhou said: "This man's form and bearing are extraordinary—I entrust my descendants to him."
translations.idiomatic: The military governor Wei Zhou gave him his brother's daughter in marriage. Others objected, but Zhou said, "This man's bearing is extraordinary. I entrust my descendants to him."

sentences.zh: 黃巢自嶺表北還，湖、湘間群盜蟻結，知謙因據封州，有詔即授刺史兼賀水鎮使，以遏梧、桂。

translations.literal: Huang Chao returned north from Lingbiao; bandit groups in Hu and Xiang clustered like ants; Zhiqian thereby seized Fengzhou; an edict at once appointed him prefect and concurrently commander of He River garrison to check Wu and Gui.
translations.idiomatic: When Huang Chao marched north from Lingnan, bandits swarmed through Hunan and the Xiang region. Zhiqian seized Fengzhou and received an edict appointing him prefect and commander of the He River garrison to block Wuzhou and Guilin.

sentences.zh: 知謙撫納流亡，愛嗇用度，養士卒。

translations.literal: Zhiqian comforted and received the displaced, was frugal in expenditures, and nurtured soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: Zhiqian welcomed refugees, husbanded his resources, and trained his troops.

sentences.zh: 未幾，得精兵萬人，多具戰艦，境內肅然。

translations.literal: Before long he obtained ten thousand seasoned troops, equipped many warships, and within his borders all was orderly.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he mustered ten thousand seasoned troops, built a strong fleet, and brought order to his territory.

sentences.zh: 久之，疾病，召諸子曰：「今五嶺盜賊方興，吾有精甲犀械，爾勉建功，時哉不可失也！」

translations.literal: After a long while he fell ill; he summoned his sons and said: "Now bandits are rising in the Five Ridges; I have fine armor and rhinoceros gear—you must strive to achieve merit; the time cannot be lost!"
translations.idiomatic: In time he fell ill and summoned his sons. "Banditry is rising in the Five Ridges," he said. "I have left you fine armor and war elephants. Strive for achievement—the moment will not wait!"

sentences.zh: 知謙卒，共推其子隱為嗣，清海軍節度使劉崇龜表為封州刺史。

translations.literal: When Zhiqian died, all pressed his son Yin as successor; Qinghai military governor Liu Chonggui memorialized to appoint him prefect of Fengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhiqian died, his followers acclaimed his son Liu Yin as successor. The Qinghai military governor Liu Chonggui petitioned to confirm Yin as prefect of Fengzhou.

sentences.zh: 嗣薛王知柔代領節度，未至，而牙將盧琚叛。

translations.literal: The heir Prince of Xue Zhīróu was to take over the military governorship but had not yet arrived when the guards officer Lu Ju rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: The heir Prince of Xue, Zhirou, was appointed to succeed to the command but had not yet arrived when the guards officer Lu Ju rebelled.

sentences.zh: 隱率兵奉迎知柔，直趨廣州，禽琚獻之。

translations.literal: Yin led troops to welcome Zhirou, pressed straight to Guangzhou, captured Ju and presented him.
translations.idiomatic: Yin marched to welcome Zhirou, drove straight on Guangzhou, captured Lu Ju, and presented him as a prisoner.

sentences.zh: 於是知柔以聞，昭宗拜隱本軍行軍司馬，俄遷副使。

translations.literal: Thereupon Zhirou reported it; Emperor Zhaozong appointed Yin army campaign marshal of this command; shortly he was transferred to deputy commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Zhirou reported the deed to court. Emperor Zhaozong appointed Yin campaign marshal of the command, then shortly promoted him to deputy commissioner.

sentences.zh: 天復初，節度徐彥若死，隱自稱留後。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianfu, military governor Xu Yanruo died; Yin styled himself acting governor.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Tianfu the military governor Xu Yanruo died, and Yin proclaimed himself acting governor.

sentences.zh: 盧光稠

translations.literal: Lu Guangchou
translations.idiomatic: Lu Guangchou

sentences.zh: 虔人盧光稠者，有眾數萬，據州自為留後，又取韶州。

translations.literal: Lu Guangchou of Qianzhou had a host of several tens of thousands, held the prefecture and styled himself acting governor, and also took Shaozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Guangchou of Qianzhou commanded tens of thousands of men, held the prefecture as self-proclaimed acting governor, and also seized Shaozhou.

sentences.zh: 隱與爭之，戰不勝，悉師攻虔州。

translations.literal: Yin contended with him, could not win in battle, and led the whole army to attack Qianzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yin fought him but could not prevail and marched his entire force against Qianzhou.

sentences.zh: 光稠伏軍掉戰，隱縱驅，伏發，挺身免。

translations.literal: Guangchou ambushed troops and feigned retreat; Yin drove forward in pursuit; the ambush sprang; he threw himself forward and escaped.
translations.idiomatic: Guangchou laid an ambush and feigned retreat. Yin pressed the pursuit, the trap closed, and he barely escaped with his life.

sentences.zh: 天祐初，始詔隱權節度留後，乃遣使者入朝，重賂朱全忠以自固。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianyou an edict at last appointed Yin acting military governor; he then sent envoys to attend court and richly bribed Zhu Quanzhong to secure himself.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Tianyou an edict at last confirmed Yin as acting military governor. He sent envoys to court and lavished gifts on Zhu Quanzhong to secure his position.

sentences.zh: 是歲，光稠死，子延昌自稱刺史，為其下所殺，更推李圖總州事。

translations.literal: That year Guangchou died; his son Yanchang styled himself prefect and was killed by his subordinates; they then pressed Li Tu to oversee prefectural affairs.
translations.idiomatic: That year Guangchou died. His son Yanchang proclaimed himself prefect but was killed by his own men, who then installed Li Tu to govern the prefecture.

sentences.zh: 圖死，鍾傳盡劫其眾，欲遣子匡時守之。

translations.literal: When Tu died, Zhong Chuan plundered his entire host and wished to send his son Kuangshi to guard it.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Tu died, Zhong Chuan seized his entire force and meant to post his son Kuangshi as garrison commander.

sentences.zh: 不克，州人自立譚全播為刺史，附全忠云。

translations.literal: He could not succeed; the people of the prefecture installed Tan Quanbo themselves as prefect and attached themselves to Quanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: He failed to hold the city. The people of the prefecture installed Tan Quanbo as prefect and submitted to Zhu Quanzhong.
